Outpost control van is near the Center of the image, left of the hanger.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/2/26/Airstrip_Base_Overview.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/356?cb=20250416193820)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/2/26/Airstrip_Base_Overview.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20250416193820)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Airstrip_Base_Overview.jpg](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Airstrip_Base_Overview.jpg)

Airstrip Base viewed facing north east. Aircraft workbench located inside of the hanger next to the tower. Outpost control van is near the Center of the image, left of the hanger.

Airstrip Base is a small island with a small hangar and runway allowing for the creation of a small plane.

"Features a hanger and runway." Stormworks Base Description

## Features

The site can be purchased for $30,000, granting access to its aircraft workbench for editing small aircraft of up to 15.75 m (63 blocks) L x 17.75m (71 blocks) W x 5.25 m (21 blocks) tall. It has a Diesel Fuel, Jet Fuel, and Electricity anchors, alongside mineral storage. The island also has 1 bed and a wardrobe in the building next to the control tower.

This base does not spawn any trailers or containers to sell

With the [Weapons DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Weapons_DLC), Airstrip Base also features an outpost control van. If the site is captured by the enemy, enemy vehicles will spawn at Airstrip Base until the player captures the site by clearing nearby enemies and staying in the van until the site reaches 100% captured. Note that the player can still purchase the Airstrip Base to spawn vehicles using the aircraft workbench even if has been captured by the enemy; they just risk being shot at in the process.

title: Arctic
summary: The Arctic is a region far to the north of the rest of the Stormworks map. It is a cold, wintry climate, and spending too long here without protection against the cold can be detrimental to the player. The Arctic contains few landmarks and inhabited structures, with few roads and very few railways. The islands are mostly rocky and covered in snow, and the seas are full of icebergs.

images.alt: The main islands in the Arctic
ArcTech Survey Base, situated on an iceberg
SGK Research Outpost, the only hospital in the Arctic

content.markdown:
## Overview

[![The main islands in the Arctic](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/8/86/ArcticMainland.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20230629085628)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/8/86/ArcticMainland.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20230629085628)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:ArcticMainland.jpg](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:ArcticMainland.jpg)

The main islands in the Arctic

The Arctic is a region far to the north of the rest of the Stormworks map. It is a cold, wintry climate, and spending too long here without protection against the cold can be detrimental to the player. The Arctic contains few landmarks and inhabited structures, with few roads and very few railways. The islands are mostly rocky and covered in snow, and the seas are full of icebergs.

Only three of the islands have roads on them, meaning land transport is not very useful. The largest island has two rail terminals, and the three smallest islands also have rail connections. The railways all link to a very long bridge that connects to the other landmasses in the south.

The Ambient Temperature is -15°c which is low enough to start damaging the player, this can be avoided by wearing an Arctic outfit or being near a Heat Source (I.E: Heaters, Fire, Fireboxes, Furnaces, and Nuclear Reactors)

## Layout

In total, there are ten islands proper in the Arctic. All other surfaces are icebergs, floating on the ocean's surface.

- The largest island is in the center of the Arctic. It has roads, and is the only major island with rail access.
- The second largest island is in the south-west of the Arctic. It is barren, apart from [Mount Paradize](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Volcano)
- Taijin Island is situated to the north-west of the largest island, and is occupied entirely by an airstrip.
- There are two smaller islands between Taijin Island and the largest island, with nothing on them apart from two roads.
- Magnus Island is to the south of the Arctic, being on the route of the rail bridge that connects the Arctic with the rest of the map.
- xFury Island is to the east of the Arctic, with a rail bridge linking it to the rest of the railways.
- Daylight Island and BVG Island are to the north of the Arctic, with rail bridges linking them to the rest of the railways.

## Landmarks and Structures

The Arctic has few landmarks and structures, most being destinations rather than waypoints. The only landmark is Mount Paradize, being visible from quite far away, but due to the scale of the arctic and size of the icebergs, it is often not visible.

### Structures

[![ArcTech Survey Base, situated on an iceberg](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/b/b5/ArcTech.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20230629085630)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/b/b5/ArcTech.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20230629085630)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:ArcTech.jpg](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:ArcTech.jpg)

ArcTech Survey Base, situated on an iceberg

- ArcTech Survey Base is a scientific outpost on an iceberg in the north of the Arctic, and resembles the [Halley VI Reseach Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halley_Research_Station) in the Antarctic.
- Arcturus is a small hamlet, seemingly the only civilian village in the Arctic. It is home to a lighthouse.
- BVG Logistics Depot is a harbor with rail and sea access in the north of the Arctic. [Shipping containers](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Shipping_container) can be found here, and it is home to a diesel gantry. Vehicles can't be made here.
- Daylight Oil Refinery is an industrial installation in the north of the Arctic with rail and sea access. It is home to an oil gantry, a diesel gantry, and a jet fuel gantry. Vehicles can't be made here.
- Krail Oilworks is an insdustrial installation on the main island with road and sea access. It is home to an oil data vendor and an oil gantry. Vehicles can't be made here.

[![SGK Research Outpost, the only hospital in the Arctic](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/4/4d/SGKHospital.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20230629085629)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/4/4d/SGKHospital.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20230629085629)

content.markdown:
## Overview

The Arid Island is a large group of landmass situated in the south of the map in Stormworks available to players with the [Industrial Frontier DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Industrial_Frontier_DLC). Often referred to as "Arid" by players. The Arid Island is part of the Industrial Frontier DLC. Arid Island contain numerous landmarks and structures, many connected by [rails](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Rails).

Arid Island is covered in [rails](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Rails), with comparatively fewer roads present. There are many major landmarks on the Arid Islands including a run down power plant, several airports/landing strips and a launch site for space vehicles.

The default starting location for players with the Industrial Frontier DLC is [North Meier Outpost](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/North_Meier_Outpost).

title: Astronomy Sensor
summary: The Astronomy Sensor is the primary tool for navigation in space. It outputs a special format of coordinates in a composite signal. Just pointing your rocket at the moon at full throttle isn't optimal in any sense (It wastes fuel and time), so using the astronomy sensor can help getting the optimal trajectory.

sections.title: The X, Y and Z component

content.markdown:
## Overview

The Astronomy Sensor is the primary tool for navigation in space. It outputs a special format of coordinates in a composite signal. Just pointing your rocket at the moon at full throttle isn't optimal in any sense (It wastes fuel and time), so using the astronomy sensor can help getting the optimal trajectory.

## The X, Y and Z component

The Y value indicates your distance to Earth. On earth's surface, this value is approximately 0, and on the moon, it is 1.

The X and Z coordinates are also important, because you do not want to miss the moon. To arrive there, you need to roughly achieve the coordinates X=0, Y=1, Z=0.

The coordinate values generated by the astronomy sensor (found in composite channels 1, 2 and 3 respectively) are similar to GPS coordinates. Because the moon is approximately 500km above Earth, you can convert from astronomy sensor coordinates to GPS coordinates that line up with Earth coordinates.

`x = astronomy_x * 490196`

`y (altitude) = astronomy_y * 490196`

z = astronomy_z * 490196

### Calculating speed

You can calculate your velocity by using a delta logic gate in the Microcontroller Editor to measure the rate of change of your coordinates. **Important:** This results in a value measured in meters per tick. To convert to m/s, you simply need to multiply it by 60. You can use the Pythagorean theorem to measure your total velocity, rather than your per-axis velocity:

`speed = sqrt(velocity_x^2+velocity_y^2+velocity_z^2)`

summary: BVG Logistics Depot viewed facing west. Diesel fuel sale gantry is at the end of the pier on the right.

images.alt: BVG Logistics Depot viewed facing west. Diesel fuel sale gantry is at the end of the pier on the right.

content.markdown:
[![BVG Logistics Depot viewed facing west. Diesel fuel sale gantry is at the end of the pier on the right.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/2/23/BVG_Logistics_Depot.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/356?cb=20220217190304)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/2/23/BVG_Logistics_Depot.png/revision/latest?cb=20220217190304)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:BVG_Logistics_Depot.png](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:BVG_Logistics_Depot.png)

BVG Logistics Depot viewed facing west. Diesel fuel sale gantry is at the end of the pier on the right.

BVG Logistics Depot is a non-purchasable island in the arctic.

## Features

It has a freight area for picking up and dropping off [shipping containers](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Shipping_container) which can be brought in/out by ship or by rail. Since it is the only freight terminal in the arctic, each of its shipping containers can be transported south for prices ranging from (at least) as little as $18,000 to as much as $46,000.

[Diesel fuel](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Game_Mechanics/Fuel#Diesel) can also be sold here at a high price (about $5/L) at the pump crane near the water. The winch for its fuel hose offers enough slack to reach the train terminals directly.

Note that the large building with the green roof is heated but does not have any beds, so it is not possible to skip time here to wait for better weather unless you have a bed on your own vehicle to do so. Since there are no vehicle spawning facilities, there is no way to refuel or repair your vehicle here unless you've brought your own supplies to do so.

## Specifications

content.markdown:
"A gimbal camera with video output feed. Has an infrared mode as well as pivot controls, a variable field of view."

## Notes

A [camera](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Video/Cameras) with telescopic and wide-field zoom capabilities, as well as [infrared mode](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Infrared_mode). It has a wide range of uses, including all of those for the [medium camera](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Camera_medium), though its size and cost make it a poor choice for video-guided remote control missiles.

If the camera is placed facing up or down, the pivot rotation allows the camera to turn in 360 degrees, looking in any bearing from the vehicle. The pitch rotation allows the camera to adjust its angle, allowing a search and rescue helicopter to switch between looking straight down (e.g. when lowering rescue harnesses towards people to be rescued) and looking forward, or at a downward angle (e.g. when looking for a lost swimmer), or even looking straight backward.

### Vehicle placement

Note that the arrow on the camera in the vehicle editor seems to be upside down compared to other cameras and monitors. The actual orientation isn't terribly important though as the camera can just be pitched 180 degrees to flip the orientation, then rotated 180 degrees to look in the same direction again.

The camera is generally best placed pointing up (common on ground vehicles and ships), or pointing downward (common on jets and helicopters).

### FOV / Zoom

The camera's FOV input will take values from 0-1 (anything higher or lower has no additional effect) and has a zoom range of 0.29x up to 28x zoom.

0 is the low-zoom wide field of view, with the camera seeing a 135-degree FOV (0.29x zoom). 1 is the high-zoom narrow field of view, with the camera seeing an approximately 1.43 degree FOV (0.025 radian FOV - 28x zoom). The camera's FOV setting is structured so that the number of degrees in its FOV increases evenly as the input value increases, so adding 0.5 to a low input value will add (135-1.43)*0.5 degrees to the FOV.

The following function can be used in a function block or Lua block in a [microcontroller](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Microcontroller) to convert from desired zoom (x) to the required input value for the camera:

1-(2*(180/pi)*(atan (tan ((pi/180)*(70/2.0))/x)))/(135-1.43)

The same logic can be used for adjusting camera zoom when tracking targets at a distance. Once you've picked a desirable zoom setting for 100m, you can simply divide the target's distance by 100, multiply by the desired zoom for 100m, and then input that desired zoom (x) into the function above.

### Pitch / pivot controls

Input values greater than -0.1 but less than 0.1 will make the camera stop turning. The camera's maximum turn rate is difficult to determine. At input values of 1 or -1, the camera turns at about 0.1 rps, though this appears to be slowed if power supply is less than 100%. At values of up to 100, the camera can turn extremely quickly, presumably at about 10 rps, though certainly fast enough to be difficult to measure.

## Patch history

### [V1.3.14](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V1.3.14)

- Rework - Cameras are now correctly nameable

### [V1.0.20](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V1.0.20)

- Fix - Gimbal Cameras not saving orientation correctly

### [V1.0.15](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V1.0.15)

- Fix - Gimbal camera mirrored editor arrows
- Fix - Gimbal camera laser rendering flipping in y-axis

### [V0.10.19-22](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.10.19-22)

- Fix - Recategorized cameras and speakers

### [V0.9.28-32](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.9.28-32)

- Fix - Camera feed visually not disappearing completely on signal loss
- Fix - Camera feed and lua overlay transparencies fighting

### [V0.9.1-2](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.9.1-2)

- Fix - Vehicle cameras not using graphics quality settings

### [V0.8.16-18](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.8.16-18)

- Fix - Rain and snow not displaying correctly when video camera is active
- Fix - Flickering player flashlight when video camera is active in 1st person view

### [V0.7.6-7](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.7.6-7)

- Fix - camera meshes appear correctly when flipped
- Fix - cameras now render water correctly when inside vehicle compartment
- Fix- increased medium and gimbal camera max zoom, made zoom characteristics the same for both cameras

### [V0.7.1](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.7.1)

- Feature - Added 3 camera components (small, medium and gimbal)
- Feature - New video logic type used for transferring camera and video feeds between components
- Feature - Added 4 monitor components to view camera and video feeds
  - Video logic can be chained through several scripts to layer many draw commands together, making it possible to build self-contained UI microcontrollers
- Feature - Added 2 video radio components (transmitter and receiver)
- Similar to radio antennas, but they transmit a video signal
- Quality of video signal will degrade over long distances

content.markdown:
"A camera with video output feed. Has infrared mode as well as a variable field of view."

## Notes

A [camera](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Video/Cameras) with telescopic and wide-field zoom capabilities, as well as [infrared mode](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Infrared_mode). It has a wide range of uses, including all of those for the [small camera](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Camera_small) as well as more advanced applications like being placed on a weapon turret to zoom in and track distant [radar](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Radar) contacts, allowing the player to positively identify them.

### FOV / Zoom

The camera's numeric FOV input will take values from 0-1 (anything higher or lower has no additional effect) and has a zoom range of 0.29x up to 28x zoom.

0 is the low-zoom wide field of view, with the camera seeing a 127-degree vertical FOV (0.29x zoom). 1 is the high-zoom narrow field of view, with the camera seeing an approximately 1.43 degree FOV (0.025 radian FOV - 28x zoom). The camera's FOV setting is structured so that the number of degrees in its FOV increases evenly as the input value increases, so adding 0.5 to a low input value will add (127-1.43)*0.5 degrees to the FOV.

The following function can be used in a function block or Lua block in a [microcontroller](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Microcontroller) to convert from desired zoom (x) to the required input value for the camera:

1-(2*(180/pi)*(atan (tan ((pi/180)*(70/2.0))/x)))/(127-1.43)

The formula to go back from a camera zoom to FOV is

0.700208/tan(0.0053+1.16562*x)

The formula to go from a camera input to FOV is

(1-x)*2.1893+0.025

The same logic can be used for adjusting camera zoom when tracking targets at a distance. Once you've picked a desirable zoom setting for 100m, you can simply divide the target's distance by 100, multiply by the desired zoom for 100m, and then input that desired zoom (x) into the function above.

content.markdown:
"A stabilized gimbal camera with video output feed. Has an infrared mode, variable field of view, stabilized and tracking modes."

## Notes

An advanced [camera](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Video/Cameras) with telescopic and wide-field zoom capabilities, as well as [infrared mode](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Infrared_mode), a laser rangefinder and positioning system, pivot/pitch controls for panoptic vision, as well as tracking plus stabilization features. It has a wide range of uses, including all of those for the [gimbal camera](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Camera_gimbal), and most notably it can be used as a target designation system (see detail in notes).

If the camera is placed facing up or down, the pivot rotation allows the camera to turn in 360 degrees, looking in any bearing from the vehicle. The pitch rotation allows the camera to adjust its angle, allowing a search and rescue helicopter to switch between looking straight down (e.g. when lowering rescue harnesses towards people to be rescued) and looking forward, or at a downward angle (e.g. when looking for a lost swimmer), or even looking straight backward.

### Vehicle placement

Note that the arrow on the camera in the vehicle editor seems to be upside down compared to other cameras and monitors. The actual orientation isn't terribly important though as the camera can just be pitched 180 degrees to flip the orientation, then rotated 180 degrees to look in the same direction again.

The camera is generally best placed pointing up (common on ground vehicles and ships), or pointing downward (common on jets and helicopters).

### FOV / Zoom

The camera's FOV input will take values from 0-1 (anything higher or lower has no additional effect) and has a zoom range of 0.29x up to 28x zoom.

0 is the low-zoom wide field of view, with the camera seeing a 135-degree FOV (0.29x zoom). 1 is the high-zoom narrow field of view, with the camera seeing an approximately 1.43 degree FOV (0.025 radian FOV - 28x zoom). The camera's FOV setting is structured so that the number of degrees in its FOV increases evenly as the input value increases, so adding 0.5 to a low input value will add (135-1.43)*0.5 degrees to the FOV.

The following function can be used in a function block or Lua block in a [microcontroller](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Microcontroller) to convert from desired zoom (x) to the required input value for the camera:

1-(2*(180/pi)*(atan (tan ((pi/180)*(70/2.0))/x)))/(135-1.43)

The same logic can be used for adjusting camera zoom when tracking targets at a distance. Once you've picked a desirable zoom setting for 100m, you can simply divide the target's distance by 100, multiply by the desired zoom for 100m, and then input that desired zoom (x) into the function above.

### Positioning / Target designation

The camera will output the world x, y, z coordinates of whatever is in the center of its field of view (terrain, vehicle, player, etc.) in its composite output, as long as the target is within 4,000 m. Note that the XYZ output can be confusing:

- X: Corresponds with the east/west position of the target (same as GPS X).

- Y: Corresponds with the target's altitude (*not* the same as GPS, but matches altimeter).

- Z: Corresponds with the target's north/south position (equivalent to GPS Y).

There is also a boolean channel (1) which outputs whether or not these coordinates are current. When the camera is not currently pointed at anything within 4,000 m, the last x, y, z coordinates of whatever was within range will continue to be reported, though the boolean channel allows those coordinates to be ignored.

These coordinates can be used to direct GPS-guided missiles and bombs towards hostile targets, or to aim fluid cannons at a fire to put it out, among other applications.

### Laser

When the laser is turned on, it will create a visible red line along the center of the camera's field of view. With the laser active, the camera will provide a distance to whatever the laser intersects within 4,000 m. If there is nothing within 4,000 m, the distance output will just show 4,000 m. When the laser is turned off, the distance output will show 0 m.

Laser wavelength can be set to allow other laser sensors to look for the position/vehicle located by the camera. Sensors like the laser point sensor and laser distance sensor looking at the same wavelength can detect the signal and can be used to make laser-guided missiles and bombs.

### Pitch / pivot controls

Input values greater than -0.1 but less than 0.1 will make the camera stop turning. The camera's maximum turn rate is difficult to determine. At input values of 1 or -1, the camera turns at about 0.1 rps, though this appears to be slowed if power supply is less than 100%. At values of up to 100, the camera can turn extremely quickly, presumably at about 10 rps, though certainly fast enough to be difficult to measure.

content.plain_text:
"A stabilized gimbal camera with video output feed. Has an infrared mode, variable field of view, stabilized and tracking modes."

Notes

An advanced
camera
 with telescopic and wide-field zoom capabilities, as well as
infrared mode
, a laser rangefinder and positioning system, pivot/pitch controls for panoptic vision, as well as tracking plus stabilization features. It has a wide range of uses, including all of those for the
gimbal camera
, and most notably it can be used as a target designation system (see detail in notes).

If the camera is placed facing up or down, the pivot rotation allows the camera to turn in 360 degrees, looking in any bearing from the vehicle. The pitch rotation allows the camera to adjust its angle, allowing a search and rescue helicopter to switch between looking straight down (e.g. when lowering rescue harnesses towards people to be rescued) and looking forward, or at a downward angle (e.g. when looking for a lost swimmer), or even looking straight backward.

Vehicle placement

Note that the arrow on the camera in the vehicle editor seems to be upside down compared to other cameras and monitors. The actual orientation isn't terribly important though as the camera can just be pitched 180 degrees to flip the orientation, then rotated 180 degrees to look in the same direction again.

The camera is generally best placed pointing up (common on ground vehicles and ships), or pointing downward (common on jets and helicopters).

FOV / Zoom

The camera's FOV input will take values from 0-1 (anything higher or lower has no additional effect) and has a zoom range of 0.29x up to 28x zoom.

0 is the low-zoom wide field of view, with the camera seeing a 135-degree FOV (0.29x zoom). 1 is the high-zoom narrow field of view, with the camera seeing an approximately 1.43 degree FOV (0.025 radian FOV - 28x zoom). The camera's FOV setting is structured so that the number of degrees in its FOV increases evenly as the input value increases, so adding 0.5 to a low input value will add (135-1.43)*0.5 degrees to the FOV.

The following function can be used in a function block or Lua block in a
microcontroller
 to convert from desired zoom (x) to the required input value for the camera:

1-(2*(180/pi)*(atan (tan ((pi/180)*(70/2.0))/x)))/(135-1.43)

The same logic can be used for adjusting camera zoom when tracking targets at a distance. Once you've picked a desirable zoom setting for 100m, you can simply divide the target's distance by 100, multiply by the desired zoom for 100m, and then input that desired zoom (x) into the function above.

Positioning / Target designation

The camera will output the world x, y, z coordinates of whatever is in the center of its field of view (terrain, vehicle, player, etc.) in its composite output, as long as the target is within 4,000 m. Note that the XYZ output can be confusing:

X: Corresponds with the east/west position of the target (same as GPS X).

Y: Corresponds with the target's altitude (
not
 the same as GPS, but matches altimeter).

Z: Corresponds with the target's north/south position (equivalent to GPS Y).

There is also a boolean channel (1) which outputs whether or not these coordinates are current. When the camera is not currently pointed at anything within 4,000 m, the last x, y, z coordinates of whatever was within range will continue to be reported, though the boolean channel allows those coordinates to be ignored.

These coordinates can be used to direct GPS-guided missiles and bombs towards hostile targets, or to aim fluid cannons at a fire to put it out, among other applications.

Laser

When the laser is turned on, it will create a visible red line along the center of the camera's field of view. With the laser active, the camera will provide a distance to whatever the laser intersects within 4,000 m. If there is nothing within 4,000 m,
the distance output will just show 4,000 m. When the laser is turned off, the distance output will show 0 m.

Laser wavelength can be set to allow other laser sensors to look for the position/vehicle located by the camera. Sensors like the
laser point sensor
 and
laser distance sensor
 looking at the same wavelength can detect the signal and can be used to make laser-guided missiles and bombs.

Pitch / pivot controls

Input values greater than -0.1 but less than 0.1 will make the camera stop turning. The camera's maximum turn rate is difficult to determine. At input values of 1 or -1, the camera turns at about 0.1 rps, though this appears to be slowed if power supply is less than 100%. At values of up to 100, the camera can turn extremely quickly, presumably at about 10 rps, though certainly fast enough to be difficult to measure.

content.markdown:
[![Coastguard Outpost Beginner viewed facing north west. The harbor workbench being in the green building.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/b/b3/Coastguard_Outpost_Begineer_Overview.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/356?cb=20250416182302)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/b/b3/Coastguard_Outpost_Begineer_Overview.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20250416182302)

Coastguard Outpost Beginner viewed facing north west. The harbor workbench being in the green building.

A small island with a small boathouse allowing for the creation of a small boat or submarine. It will always spawn in a pair with the St. Sebastiaz Hospital island.

"Features a small dock." Stormworks Base Description

## Features

The site can be purchased for $10,000, granting access to its a harbor workbench for editing small ships of up to *. It also comes with 1 Tractor and 1 trailer that can be driven but cannot be taken into the workbench. It also comes with an overhead crane. It has a Diesel Fuel, Jet Fuel, and Electricity anchors, alongside coal storage. You are able to turn on and off the lights, as well as shut the shutters at the back of the Green building. The island also has 1 bed and a wardrobe in the white house up the hill. Loot crates can spawn on this island.

This base does not spawn any trailers or containers to transport.

The Coastguard Outpost Beginner base is also where the game will start the tutorial, regardless if you start there or not, entering the White building will begin the tutorial. Starting the tutorial spawns in a boat in the green building. It does not take fuel or money from the base/player. This boat can be taken into the workbench, but will not yield you any money or fuel.

content.markdown:
| [![Stub](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/f/f1/Stub_v1.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/64?cb=20250514003444)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/f/f1/Stub_v1.png/revision/latest?cb=20250514003444) | *This article is a [stub](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Category:Stubs). *You can help Us by [expanding it](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Damage_control?action=edit). |
| --- | --- |

Vehicles can be damaged in Stormworks in many different ways. In the base game, there is the risk of colliding vehicles with other vehicles or terrain. Additionally, an engine which runs too fast and is inadequately cooled can overheat and catch on fire. Fire can spread to nearby walls and components causing gradually spreading damage. There are also some [missions](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Missions) which create substantial risk of vehicle damage, e.g. towing an old sea mine to a port. With the [Search and Destroy DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Search_and_Destroy_DLC), enemy vehicles may also fire guns, rockets, and missiles at player-made vehicles. With the many different ways vehicles can be damaged, it is good practice to prepare vehicles to be able to survive the damage and recover.

## Damage propagation

Damage can spread by fire, by ammunition cookoff, or by warhead detonation.

Damaged batteries and engines can catch on fire. The fire can spread across anything, even normal blocks, unless/until is extinguished. A single uncontrolled fire can eventually destroy an entire ship or aircraft.

Damaged ammo drums which contain ammo can cook off. Several rounds of whatever ammo type they contain will be shot out in random directions around the drum. Large quantities of ammo packed together can easily cause a rapid chain reaction.

Torpedo, missile, and bomb warheads can explode if they are damaged. If they are positioned near each other and one is damaged, it can lead to almost instantaneous detonation of the entire group. EMP warheads will also trigger their EMP effect if damaged.

Rocket launchers, battle cannon belts, artillery cannon belts, and Bertha cannon belts are all safe to damage without risk of chain reaction.

## Bulkheads

Dividing a large ship or submarine into several sections separated by walls along its length and width can help to contain flooding.

### Collision risk

The front of a ship is the area most likely to be damaged in a collision, so the front bulkhead area is generally the most important. To prevent fires it should not contain batteries, ammo, or fuel-driven engines. Additionally, it needs to be sized appropriately. If it's too small, the bulkhead may be damaged along with the hull, leading to further flooding behind it. Thus, it needs to be designed large enough to contain the damage but not overly large so that it remains easy to bilge out if it floods.

## Fire detection

Temperature sensors can detect the added heat of a fire. Once the sensor is broken, it will suddenly report a temperature of exactly 0. A high temperature or 0 temperature can both be taken as signs that an area is likely to have an active fire.

## Fire suppression

At the very least, nearly every vehicle should carry a fire extinguisher. A small upgrade from this for ships likely to have large fires to put out is to include a water pipe running down the length of the vessel supplied by a large pump. With numerous hose attachment points on this pipe, a player can attach a hose to one of the points and use it as a fire extinguisher with unlimited supply.

Where possible, components most likely to catch on fire if damaged, like diesel engines and batteries, should have automatic fire suppression systems. This can be accomplished with fluid cannon nozzles set to a wide spray, or with fluid cannons configured with micro-controllers to automatically spray an area. Temperature sensors can automatically detect that the area is hot (or has been damaged, which would mean probably on fire) and trigger the fluid cannons to douse the fire.

## Repair

[![Fully damaged surface repaired at the red block. Welding torch and mounted welder produce the same result.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/8/89/Welding_torch_repair.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20250819001905)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/8/89/Welding_torch_repair.png/revision/latest?cb=20250819001905)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Welding_torch_repair.png](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Welding_torch_repair.png)

Fully damaged surface repaired at the red block. Welding torch and mounted welder produce the same result.

Repair can be done with by hand with welders or underwater welders, or with a vehicle using mounted welders. Most vehicles should have at least a welder and underwater welder for basic manual repairs. Mounted welders use large amounts of electricity but can be run semi-autonomously, e.g. placed on a track and moved down the the length of a ship to weld everything damaged along the hull. They can also reach places that are too small for a player to get into, e.g. a 2x2 tunnel through a ship could fit a compact rail and several welders that weld everything in all directions around the length of the tunnel.

### Lingering effects

Even after being repaired, batteries will still be depleted. Ammo drums that cooked off will be depleted of ammo.

Note that fluid tanks and gas tanks will *not* lose their contents if damaged. Also, warheads that were part of a vehicle/subvehicle which was not too damaged to continue existing can be repaired and detonated again.

## Redundancy

For critical systems, like power, it's generally a good idea to have a redundant backup.

For example, note that a damaged battery will still have zero power after repair. If you needed the battery to start your engine and needed the engine to charge your battery, then you may be left with an inoperable vehicle that you can't get working again. Having a backup battery in a separate location and a circuit breaker to protect it against being drained will allow you to fix your damaged main battery, restart your engine, and then recharge both batteries.

### Manual backups

Hand cranks can be a very useful way to either manually crank an engine to start (if the starter has insufficient power), or to provide initial charge to a battery so basic systems like throttles, buttons, clutches, and starters can be used.

Be aware that clutches do not work without power and they are commonly used to limit power taken by generators. If there's only one battery and one generator and the generator takes power from the engine through a clutch then in the event of battery damage there will be no way to get the vehicle running again unless/until it can be jumpstarted. For this typical situation, it is good practice to have one or two handcranks connected to the generator *after* the clutch.

Note that hand cranks turn slowly, usually less than 1 rpm, but have decent torque. Three [gearboxes](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Guides/Gearbox) set to 3:1 with the arrows facing towards the handcrank(s) and a small generator are an effective way to recharge a small battery enough to start an engine within a few minutes.

### Auxiliary power units (APUs)

See [auxiliary power unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auxiliary_power_unit) at Wikipedia.

Many real-life aircraft carry an engine and generator solely dedicated to providing power for the aircraft. As the name suggests, this is a dedicated backup system. Generators connected to the main engines provide all power under normal circumstances, although the APU may be used to initially power up the aircraft before takeoff if ground power is unavailable. Further, in the event of simultaneous engine failure, the APU can be switched on in-flight to maintain power to control surfaces, fuel pumps, landing gear hydraulics, de-icing systems, and life support to buy time for the engine failure to be diagnosed and corrected, or, if all else fails, to at least facilitate an attempted [deadstick landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadstick_landing).

For Stormworks, much of the same logic applies. If an aircraft has just one battery at the bottom of the hull and it gets hit by a single round of ammo from a rotary autocannon, the engines will likely shut down in most designs, because:

- If a throttle is used to control engine throttle, an unpowered throttle will suddenly output 0, resulting in engine shutdown.

- If a clutch is used, an unpowered clutch will stop working resulting in total loss of power transmission from the engine to the rotor / propellers.

- If any electric [pumps](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Pumps) are used (e.g. pumps acting as superchargers/turbochargers), these will shut down, blocking all air flow to the engine.

In addition to likely loss of engine power, all control surfaces will shut down, landing gears will be inoperable, pumps for fire suppression systems will not run, and mounted welders will be unable to repair the situation. With a backup battery, electric relay, backup generator, and appropriate microcontroller, the aircraft could automatically get power back on, extinguish the fire(s), and repair the main battery along with any other critical systems protected by mounted welders.

Note that a basic APU can be made with a small diesel engine, a gearbox set at 3:2 (arrows facing the engine), and a medium generator. The generator will produce 36 swatts while the engine will run at 8.16 rps and consume 0.06L of diesel per second. The power is a bit more than enough to run one mounted welder at a time.

## External links

[Casual Navigation: Why Didn't This Ship Sink After Crashing?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tpBUdsXNAaQ)

title: Equipment
summary: Stormworks has a variety of equipment, including outfits, tools, weapons, and gadgets with a wide variety of uses. Players have 8 small equipment slots, 1 large equipment slot, and 1 outfit slot. Carrying equipment reduces move speed in proportion to its weight.

content.markdown:
Stormworks has a variety of equipment, including outfits, tools, weapons, and gadgets with a wide variety of uses. Players have 8 small equipment slots, 1 large equipment slot, and 1 outfit slot. Carrying equipment reduces move speed in proportion to its weight.

A lot of equipment is battery-operated and can be recharged by putting it back into an equipment rack which has power available; some non-battery operated equipment also can be replenished when put into a powered equipment rack, like oxygen masks.

## Small Equipment

Small equipment fits into a 1x1 equipment rack. Players can carry eight items of small equipment at a time.

- **Flashlight:** Replaced the pre-1.0 Headlamp. Battery-powered, shines a cone of light ahead of you. Recharges slowly in a powered locker.
- **Binoculars:** Allows you to zoom in further. Doesn't use power or require charging.
- **First Aid Kit:** Heals you, other players, or NPCs. Maximum (also default) stack of 4, consumable. Each use restores about half of a full health bar for a player or NPC, or a full health bar for a [Stormwoof](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormwoof).
- **Night Vision Binoculars:** Battery-powered, allows you to zoom in with [night vision](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Infrared_mode). Does not allow regular vision.
- **Oxygen Mask:** Allows you to breathe in an environment without oxygen or excessive CO2, but much more limited capacity than SCUBA or diving gear. It offers 10 breaths, approximately enough for two minutes. Left click needed to breathe. Quickly refills when in a powered locker.
- **Compass:** Has two needles, the white points south, the red points north. Doesn't use power or require charging. Shows you what bearing you are facing in degrees shown above the compass' position in the equipment slot where it was placed.
- **Radio:** Battery-powered; can be used to chat with other players on the same channel (limited to channels 0-8) with a maximum effective range of 500 meters. Can also be used to signal vehicles with speakers (which produce an on/off output when receiving voice data from a linked radio channel), allowing for limited [radio](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Workbench/Components/Radio) control.
- **Remote Control Unit:** Battery-powered; allows you to remotely control a vehicle (as long as you set it up correctly). Limited to using radio channels 0-8, and an effective range of up to 500 meters.
- **Glowstick:** Provides hands-free illumination, works underwater. Lasts for somewhere between 25-30 minutes. Maximum (also default) stack of 12.
- **Flare:** Allows you to throw a road flare, provides very bright hands-free illumination, works underwater. Lasts for five minutes. Maximum (also default) stack of 4, consumable.
- **Flare Gun Ammo:** Maximum (also default) stack of 4. Used for reloading the Flare Gun. Can be refilled by unloading the Flare Gun, consumable.
- **Flare Gun:** Fires a flare in the direction you are facing (usually with an angle limit), contains one flare by default. Can be unloaded to refill Flare Gun Ammo (if you have it equipped).
- **Transponder:** Battery-powered, transmits a transponder signal, can be switched to MOB mode to activate automatically in water, has a battery meter
- **Strobe Light:** Battery-powered, model identical to transponder, flashes a strobe light when turned on, has a battery meter. Can be set to MOB (man overboard) mode like the transponder.
- **Strobe Light (IR):** Model identical to transponder, flashes a strobe light in [IR](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Infrared_mode) when turned on, has a battery meter. Can be set to MOB mode like the regular strobe light and transponder.
- **Radiation Detector:** A small battery-operated Geiger counter.

### Weapon DLC

The [Weapon DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_DLC) added:

- **Pistol:** A short-ranged semi-automatic pistol with a magazine capacity of 17 rounds.
- **C4 Explosive:** Can be placed on vehicles or terrain and remotely detonated.
- **C4 Detonator:** Remotely detonates any C4 placed by the player.
- **Hand Grenade:** Can be thrown a short distance - only accurate when standing still and throwing. Detonates after a short delay.
- **Pistol ammo:** An extra 17-round pistol magazine, Consumable.
- **SMG ammo:** An extra 40-round SMG magazine, Consumable.
- **Rifle ammo:** An extra 30-round rifle magazine, Consumable.
- **Speargun ammo:** Maximum(also default) stacked by 8 of speargun ammo, Consumable.

## Large Equipment

Large equipment fits in a 3x1 equipment rack. Players can only carry one item of large equipment at a time.

- **Fire Extinguisher:** Puts out fires. Carries a maximum of 9L of water and cannot be refilled.
- **Cable:** Can connect to two electric connectors. Useful for jump-starting a vehicle with a dead battery or for creating a wired data transfer link.
- **[Rope](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Rope):** Can connect two rope anchors to each other. Most commonly used for towing boats, cars, and trucks. Can also be used to winch a player into a helicopter while carrying a [survivor](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Survivor), among many other possibilities.
- **Hose:** Can connect two liquid hose anchors to each other. Can also be used as a fire hose if it is a connected to a fluid nozzle with a pump supplying water.
- **Defibrillator:** Can revive incapacitated players and NPCs, has four charges, and can be recharged by placing in an equipment storage rack.
- **Welder:** Can fix components, cannot be used underwater, has 400 units of fuel, and cannot be refilled.
- **Underwater Welder:** Can fix components, works underwater, but has only 250 units of fuel compared to the welder and repairs slower.
- **Radio Signal Locator:** Battery powered; The name is deceptive. It does not detect radio signals, but will detect transponder signals and beeps faster as it gets closer to the source.
- **Fishing rod:** Used for catching fish which can be sold. A relaxing way to earn some extra money in [career](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Gamemodes/Career) or [classic](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Gamemodes/Classic) mode.

### Weapon DLC

The [Weapon DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_DLC) added:

- **Rifle:** An automatic rifle with a 30-round magazine. Accuracy is decent when firing single shots or short bursts, but very poor when firing continuously.
- **SMG:** A 40-round fully automatic submachine gun. Accuracy and range is poorer than with the rifle, but it is nonetheless effective in close quarters.
- **Speargun:** A single-shot weapon which works underwater.

## Outfits

Outfits fit in a 3x3 equipment rack. Players can only wear one outfit at a time.

- **Firefighting Gear:** Reduces fire damage by 95%.
- **Firefighting SCBA:** Reduces fire damage by 95% with a air tank, can be used in enclosed space for fire extinguishing, Slowly refills in a locker with oxygen connected
- **SCUBA Gear:** Allows you to breathe underwater for an extended period of time, increases dive depth, slowly refills in a locker with oxygen connected.
- **Diving Gear:** Better SCUBA gear with better pressure endurance, at the cost of slightly reduced visibility. Slowly refills in a locker with oxygen connected.
- **Parachute:** Allows slow falling by deploying when at high speed, can only be used once, though it repacks itself when placed in body equipment locker.
- **Arctic Gear:** Significantly slows the effects of low temperatures, such as in the Arctic or at very high altitudes.
- **HAZMAT Gear:** Reduces effects of radiation by 95%.
- **SPACE SUIT:** Provides O2 in space and has a temporary jetpack which uses up your O2, Slowly refills in a locker with oxygen connected

## Patch history

- [V1.0.0](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V1.0.0) 15 new pieces of equipment were added, including slots for small and large equipment.
- [V0.4.36](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.4.34-36) Parachutes were added.
- [V0.4.1](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.4.1) Equipment was added to the game, limited to just outfits.

Can also be used to signal vehicles with speakers (which produce an on/off output when receiving voice data from a linked radio channel), allowing for limited [[Gameplay/Workbench/Components/Radio|radio]] control.
* '''Remote Control Unit:''' Battery-powered; allows you to remotely control a vehicle (as long as you set it up correctly). Limited to using radio channels 0-8, and an effective range of up to 500 meters.
* '''Glowstick:''' Provides hands-free illumination, works underwater. Lasts for somewhere between 25-30 minutes. Maximum (also default) stack of 12.
* '''Flare:''' Allows you to throw a road flare, provides very bright hands-free illumination, works underwater. Lasts for five minutes. Maximum (also default) stack of 4, consumable.
* '''Flare Gun Ammo:''' Maximum (also default) stack of 4. Used for reloading the Flare Gun. Can be refilled by unloading the Flare Gun, consumable.
* '''Flare Gun:''' Fires a flare in the direction you are facing (usually with an angle limit), contains one flare by default. Can be unloaded to refill Flare Gun Ammo (if you have it equipped).
* '''Transponder:''' Battery-powered, transmits a transponder signal, can be switched to MOB mode to activate automatically in water, has a battery meter
* '''Strobe Light:''' Battery-powered, model identical to transponder, flashes a strobe light when turned on, has a battery meter. Can be set to MOB (man overboard) mode like the transponder.
* '''Strobe Light (IR):''' Model identical to transponder, flashes a strobe light in [[infrared mode|IR]] when turned on, has a battery meter. Can be set to MOB mode like the regular strobe light and transponder.
* '''Radiation Detector:''' A small battery-operated Geiger counter.

=== Weapon DLC ===
The [[Weapon DLC]] added:

* '''Pistol:''' A short-ranged semi-automatic pistol with a magazine capacity of 17 rounds.
* '''C4 Explosive:''' Can be placed on vehicles or terrain and remotely detonated.
* '''C4 Detonator:''' Remotely detonates any C4 placed by the player.
* '''Hand Grenade:''' Can be thrown a short distance - only accurate when standing still and throwing. Detonates after a short delay.
* '''Pistol ammo:''' An extra 17-round pistol magazine, Consumable.
* '''SMG ammo:''' An extra 40-round SMG magazine, Consumable.
* '''Rifle ammo:''' An extra 30-round rifle magazine, Consumable.
* '''Speargun ammo:''' Maximum(also default) stacked by 8 of speargun ammo, Consumable.

== Large Equipment ==
Large equipment fits in a 3x1 equipment rack. Players can only carry one item of large equipment at a time.

* '''Fire Extinguisher:''' Puts out fires. Carries a maximum of 9L of water and cannot be refilled.
* '''Cable:''' Can connect to two electric connectors. Useful for jump-starting a vehicle with a dead battery or for creating a wired data transfer link.
* '''[[Rope]]:''' Can connect two rope anchors to each other. Most commonly used for towing boats, cars, and trucks. Can also be used to winch a player into a helicopter while carrying a [[survivor]], among many other possibilities.
* '''Hose:''' Can connect two liquid hose anchors to each other. Can also be used as a fire hose if it is a connected to a fluid nozzle with a pump supplying water.
* '''Defibrillator:''' Can revive incapacitated players and NPCs, has four charges, and can be recharged by placing in an equipment storage rack.
* '''Welder:''' Can fix components, cannot be used underwater, has 400 units of fuel, and cannot be refilled.
* '''Underwater Welder:''' Can fix components, works underwater, but has only 250 units of fuel compared to the welder and repairs slower.
* '''Radio Signal Locator:''' Battery powered; The name is deceptive. It does not detect radio signals, but will detect transponder signals and beeps faster as it gets closer to the source.
* '''Fishing rod:''' Used for catching fish which can be sold. A relaxing way to earn some extra money in [[Gameplay/Gamemodes/Career|career]] or [[Gameplay/Gamemodes/Classic|classic]] mode.

=== Weapon DLC ===
The [[Weapon DLC]] added:

* '''Rifle:''' An automatic rifle with a 30-round magazine. Accuracy is decent when firing single shots or short bursts, but very poor when firing continuously.
* '''SMG:''' A 40-round fully automatic submachine gun. Accuracy and range is poorer than with the rifle, but it is nonetheless effective in close quarters.
* '''Speargun:''' A single-shot weapon which works underwater.

== Outfits ==
Outfits fit in a 3x3 equipment rack. Players can only wear one outfit at a time.

* '''Firefighting Gear:''' Reduces fire damage by 95%.
* '''Firefighting SCBA:''' Reduces fire damage by 95% with a air tank, can be used in enclosed space for fire extinguishing, Slowly refills in a locker with oxygen connected
* '''SCUBA Gear:''' Allows you to breathe underwater for an extended period of time, increases dive depth, slowly refills in a locker with oxygen connected.
* '''Diving Gear:''' Better SCUBA gear with better pressure endurance, at the cost of slightly reduced visibility. Slowly refills in a locker with oxygen connected.
* '''Parachute:''' Allows slow falling by deploying when at high speed, can only be used once, though it repacks itself when placed in body equipment locker.
* '''Arctic Gear:''' Significantly slows the effects of low temperatures, such as in the Arctic or at very high altitudes.
* '''HAZMAT Gear:''' Reduces effects of radiation by 95%.
* '''SPACE SUIT:''' Provides O2 in space and has a temporary jetpack which uses up your O2, Slowly refills in a locker with oxygen connected

== Patch history ==
* [[V1.0.0]] 15 new pieces of equipment were added, including slots for small and large equipment.
* [[V0.4.34-36|V0.4.36]] Parachutes were added.
* [[V0.4.1]] Equipment was added to the game, limited to just outfits.

title: FAQ
summary: Stormworks uses Steam networking, so all you need is to host a game and your friends can join to you (or you can invite them). Just like in many other games on Steam.

content.markdown:
## Common

**How to play multiplayer?**

Stormworks uses Steam networking, so all you need is to host a game and your friends can join to you (or you can invite them). Just like in many other games on Steam.

**Why am I or my friends unable to connect?**

In most of the cases there shouldn’t be any issues, because modern firewalls can automatically allow all needed connections.

But, if your friends can’t see your game, then you should change settings of your firewall to allow Steam inbound and outbound connections.

If your friends can see your game, but can’t join (“Waiting for server...” message) then you should allow inbound and outbound connections for Stormworks game.

**Why is there multiplayer lag?**

Currently the server runs at the speed of the slowest client, so it is normal for the game to become slow if someone joins the game who has a PC that is below min spec. As of major update #10 ([https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/573090/view/3585365461714494855](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/573090/view/3585365461714494855)), Multiplayer no longer runs at the speed of the slowest client.

**What are the system requirements?**

CPU: Intel i5 4th Generation (Intel i7 6th Generation recommended)*

RAM: 8GB

GPU: Intel HD 6000 / GeForce 550 (GeForce 750 / Radeon R7 360 recommended)**

OS: Windows 7 / 8 / 10, MacOS

- CPU matters much more in most cases, since it’s a sandbox game based on physics simulation. The larger and more complex the vehicle you spawn (or the greater number of vehicles), the more time and resources will be spent on physics calculations.
  - Graphics card must support OpenGL 3.2 or higher

**How to report a bug?**

We strongly recommend you use the Report a Bug button which you can find in the top right corner of the in-game menu. This logs you in so you can upvote, create posts, and comment.

If you wish to just view the bug tracker, click this link: [https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks)

**Where is the save folder?**

All your vehicles are saved here %appdata%\Roaming\Stormworks\data\vehicles

Your mission playlists stored here %appdata%\Roaming\Stormworks\data\missions

World saves are located here %appdata%\Roaming\Stormworks\saves

**Where is the game/minidump/log.txt folder?**

The easiest and most straight-forward way to find this is right-clicking Stormworks in Steam library then Properties > Local files > Show local files...

**What is the game engine/language?**

It’s our own engine written in C++. We use Bullet as the physics engine.

- Fix - #24217 Minor control fin art asset issues

  - - The sides of nets can be extended and contracted similar to a winch

title: Flare Launcher
summary:
Flare Launchers are vehicle-mounted systems to deploy flares. They are one-time-use and cannot be reloaded, though
hardpoints
 can be used to create disposable flare pods which can be replaced like any other ordnance.
attributes_markdown:
## Specifications

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Name | Flare Launcher |
| Image | 200px |
| Mass | 1 |
| Dimensions | 1×1×1 |
| Cost | $10 |
| Logic inputs | Boolean (Launch) |
| Logic outputs | Boolean (Launch passthrough) |
| Connections | None (No power required) |

content.markdown:
Flare Launchers are vehicle-mounted systems to deploy flares. They are one-time-use and cannot be reloaded, though [hardpoints](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Hardpoint) can be used to create disposable flare pods which can be replaced like any other ordnance.

Deployed flares last for three minutes. They can be picked up by hand without injury and do not risk igniting vehicles.

Flares can be used for illumination during nighttime search-and-rescue operations (e.g. when trying to find stranded swimmers). They can also be used for signalling, providing a way for vehicles to report their position.

[Infrared](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Infrared_mode) flares can be used to provide illumination for infrared [cameras](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Video/Cameras). These flares have about 1/4 the normal visible illumination, but still retain full visibility in infrared.

## Flare types

- Illumination: Provides bright illumination over a wide area but quickly falls to the ground. Can be used for signalling, including alerting rescuers to your location.

- Smoke: Provides some illumination and creates a billowing cloud of smoke. Can be used by aircraft to mark ground locations for rescuers to go to, as the smoke can be seen over terrain obstacles.

- Illumination parachute: Like an illumination flare, but falls slowly, providing good area lighting for a while. Excellent source of illumination for nighttime search-and-rescue operations (e.g. when trying to find stranded swimmers), especially as several can be spread over a wide area.

- Smoke parachute: Like the smoke flare but falls slowly. Largely decorative use, though can be used as a crude wind gauge.

- Chaff: Looks like a faintly sparkling cloud. Can be detected by [radar](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Radar), and if it is closer than the vehicle it was launched from, it will appear as the first target, potentially causing missiles to go off course and auto-turrets to aim into the air. Unlike the other options, chaff clouds only last about six seconds.

## Logic

Flares will launch when they receive an 'on' signal. They can be daisy-chained by connecting the launch passthrough output to the next flare launcher. When an empty flare launcher receives an 'on' signal, its launch passthrough will be set to on to launch the next flare. A blinker can be used to cause repeated flare launches, such as if sustained chaff is required.

content.markdown:
Fluid jets are a form of [propulsion](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Propulsion) with built-in [thrust pivoting](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Vehicles/Water/Boat#Thrust_pivoting) ability. They are an especially good choice for making high-speed watercraft. Despite the generic term "fluid", fluid jets actually only work with seawater - other fluids will not be expelled.

## Fluid requirements

Fluid jets can work without a fluid pump at all, simply using their supplied power to move fluid as necessary as long as the fluid intake port is connected to a fluid source. Pumps can be used to increase the fluid supply to the jet to prevent sputtering / intermittent operation.

## Power requirements

- Small engines are not recommended for fluid jets - they struggle to provide anywhere close to the required power except with reduction gearing, high RPS, and/or low clutch settings.
- A [medium engine](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Medium_engine) at 1:1 gearing can just barely run a fluid jet while sustaining at ~2.7 RPS. They can work better with reduction gearing and/or a clutch.

## Inputs

The deflectors take values from 0-1 and convert forward thrust to lateral thrust when activated. The deflectors stay away from the fluid stream at 0, but move towards it as their input value increases.

Deflector A is on the right, deflects the stream to the right, and thus causes a vehicle to turn to the left as it is activated (if the fluid jet is located at the back of the vessel).

Deflector B is on the left, deflects the stream to the left, and thus causes a vehicle to turn to the right as it is activated (if the fluid jet is located at the back of the vessel).

Activating both deflectors in the same proportion will decrease the thrust provided by the water jet, with maximum deflector activation resulting in zero thrust.

Vertical trim takes values from -1 to 1. A vertical trim of 1 causes the water stream to be forced downwards, while -1 creates an upward stream. Assuming the fluid jet is located on the back of the vessel, +1 will create a lifting force on the back of the vessel while pitching it downward, while -1 will push the back of the vessel down but pitch the vessel upward.

Note that standard orientation is with the fluid intake port placed below the power connection, and with the deflector B logic input on the left side when viewed from the back of the ship in the vehicle editor (note that mirrored placement will cause mirroring of this orientation, so fluid jets are best to place manually). If you have fluid jets in nonstandard orientation, you will need to reverse some or all of this information.

## Patch history

### [V0.5.17-19](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.5.17-19)

- Fix - Improved water stream rendering for fluid jet
- Fix - Fixed fluid jet deflector bucket rotation direction

### [V0.5.16](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.5.16)

- Feature - Added Fluid Jet component (water jet that produces thrust and has thrust vectoring)

**Stormworks** is the game where you design and pilot your own sea-rescue service (military/industrial/space service with DLCs), in a rich and dramatic physics playground. Steer or fly your custom-designed, block based, programmable vehicles into fierce oceanic storms. Plan and execute thrilling rescues in a variety of challenging crisis scenarios.

## Gamemodes

Ever since release of Stormworks, the game had 3 gamemodes, those being:

1. [Career](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Gamemodes/Career)

A gamemode focused on earning money via delivering containers, completing missions and locating crates, then buying various hangars and making better vehicles with it.

2. [Custom](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Gamemodes/Custom)

A gamemode allowing player to set their own limitations whether that'll be limited/unlimited money, electricity, fuel and ammo, natural disasters spawned by the player or some other mechanic to aid or hinder their gameplay.

3. [Classic](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Gamemodes/Classic)

A gamemode focused on earning money via delivering containers, completing missions and collecting crates, then buying various hangars and making better vehicles with it with additional "[Research](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Research)" mechanic that requires player to find crates and complete missions to receive "Research points" that can later be used to open a category of items.

## DLCs

## Workshop

## Vehicles

There are 4 main types of vehicles a player can build, these include:

1. Boats - Utility/Naval Vessels, Cruise Ships, etc.

2. Cars - Trucks, Tanks, Exploration Vehicles, etc.

3. Planes - Props/Turboprops, Jets, V/STOL Capable Aircrafts, etc.

4. Helicopters - Rescue Helicopters, Helitankers, Delivery Helicopters, etc.

Additional types of vehicles do exist but are either mostly used for decorations, Custom mode dependent, are "Proofs of concept" or are multi-vehicles - combination of 1-4 main types of vehicles with possible additions (For example: Crane Arms).

"Proof of concept" types of vehicles focus on showcasing capabilities of microcontrollers (For example: Trajectory Calculating HUDs/HMDs) or discovered glitches that can allow players achieve infinite electricity, high speeds, etc.

## Mechanism

This game contains a complex mechanism to play, see more on [Mechanism](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Mechanics)

## World

See more on World

## Workbench

Workbench is the most common way you can build up and generate a vehicle

There are 2 types of Workbench

See more on [Workbench](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Workbench)

## Multiplayer

Although this gameplay is played in single-player by default, it supports multiplayer from clients for both hosting and joining multiplayer servers.

For detail, you can see [the main page](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Multiplayer) for more.

title: Gameplay/Gamemodes/Career
summary: The Career mode is the default way to play the game, as intended by its developers. In this mode, you start with $20,000 of starting funds at the Starter Base, which has a small workbench where you can spawn and edit small boats. Fuel is limited, and must be purchased at a gas station. If you die, you cannot respawn, but can load an older save of your world. There is no 3rd person camera, but photo mode is allowed.

content.markdown:
The Career mode is the default way to play the game, as intended by its developers. In this mode, you start with $20,000 of starting funds at the Starter Base, which has a small workbench where you can spawn and edit small boats. Fuel is limited, and must be purchased at a gas station. If you die, you cannot respawn, but can load an older save of your world. There is no 3rd person camera, but photo mode is allowed.

### Tutorial mission

The game's tutorial will start as soon as you arrive on the Starter Base. It gives you a small rescue boat and teaches you how to use equipment and how to rescue casualties and extinguish fires. It does not teach anything about vehicle building.

It can be disabled in the addons tab when creating a new world.

### Earning Money

There are several ways of earning more cash.

1. **Missions** - Missions will periodically be spawned, and after completion of each objective, a reward is granted.
2. **Containers** - At every major cargo terminal, [Shipping container](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Shipping_container)s are spawned.
3. **Fuel trading** - Some locations buy or sell fuel (Crude oil, Diesel, Jet fuel). If you have access to a large vehicle, this can be very profitable.
4. **Mining** - Some locations have ore deposits. These can be mined and sold for cash. If you don't have the Industrial DLC, you can still mine and trade coal, but you won't be able to mine and refine metals.
5. **Oil drilling** - Using specialized equipment, you can build oil rigs and drill for crude oil.
6. **Refining** - Crude oil can be refined into Diesel and Jet fuel, allowing it to be used for fuel or sold for profit.
7. **Fishing** - Fish can be collected using the ingame nets, allowing you to collect fish as you move. You can take these fish to a fish seller in order to make a profit.

title: Gameplay/Gamemodes/Classic
summary:
In classic game mode, the player starts off with limited money, parts, and fuel. Money must be earned from doing missions to afford to build vehicles, buy fuel, and buy new outposts. Research points must be obtained by collecting
loot crates
 or completing missions and can spent on
research
 to unlock parts. Note that this mode can be a good place to start for a new player since it can teach the basics with simple blocks and gradually add new blocks over time to make the game's extensive parts list less overwhelming.

content.markdown:
In classic game mode, the player starts off with limited money, parts, and fuel. Money must be earned from doing missions to afford to build vehicles, buy fuel, and buy new outposts. Research points must be obtained by collecting [loot crates](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Loot_crate) or completing missions and can spent on [research](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Research) to unlock parts. Note that this mode can be a good place to start for a new player since it can teach the basics with simple blocks and gradually add new blocks over time to make the game's extensive parts list less overwhelming.

The map starts off unexplored. The player has access to both first-person and third-person view. Respawning is available. The player cannot teleport, not even between player-owned bases.

## Starting location

Various starting locations can be chosen. Without the Industrial Frontier DLC, the default starting location is [Coastguard Outpost Beginner](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Coastguard_Outpost_Beginner), a small island with a small dock where you can build your ship.

If the player owns the Industrial Frontier DLC, the default starting location is [North Meier Outpost](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/North_Meier_Outpost). Similar to the Coastguard Outpost Beginner, this outpost offers a small dock to build your ship as well as a garage for small road vehicles and VTOLs.

## Gameplay

You'll frequently be offered missions and this is your main way of getting new blocks and materials as well as earn some cash. Alternatively, you can find loot out in the world, either floating in the ocean or on islands.

As you progress in the game, you'll discover new islands you'll be able to purchase if you have enough money, these islands will offer the ability to fast travel to them and offer a new building location. Depending on the island you bought you will be able to build larger ships, or air and ground vehicles, assuming you have the necessary building blocks.

New and more difficult missions will be offered as you unlock more islands. You can look on the map to see what missions are available so you can prepare and alter your vehicle if needed.

## Starting resources

The player starts off with $15,000 and 5 research points. There should also be 2,110L of jet fuel, 5,110L of diesel, and 100 units of coal at the starting outpost.

## Starting parts

The starting parts include:

- Basic '[blocks](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Workbench/Components/Blocks)' of all of the various sizes and shapes, including weight blocks
- Pipes of all of the various types (including enclosed pipes).
- [Windows](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Workbench/Components/Windows) of all of the various sizes and shapes (excluding portholes)
- Small [diesel engine](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Workbench/Components/Propulsion/DieselEngines)
- Small propeller
- Small electric motor
- Small generator
- Clutch
- Gearbox
- [Small battery](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Electric_battery_small)
- Electric circuit breaker
- Rudder and fin rudder
- Basic display parts, including the dial, digital display, light, and indicator light
- A searchlight
- Basic controls, including the throttle lever, push button, and toggle button
- Control seats, including the compact pilot seat, driver seat, pilot seat, pilot seat (HOTAS), saddle seat, and control handle.
- Passenger seats, including the passenger seat, saddle passenger seat, padded seat
- A bed
- Many 'fluid' parts, including the exhaust, fluid heat radiator, fluid port/port end, fluid tank small/medium, gas/liquid relief valves, and all gas tank sizes.
- Various specialist equipment including binoculars (and night vision binoculars), compass, defibrillator, dog whistle, fire extinguisher, first aid kit, fishing rod, flare, flaregun ammo, flaregun, flashlight, glowstick, oxygen mask, radio signal locator, radio, remote control unit, strobe light (and infrared version), transponder, welding torch (and underwater version)
- Ropes, cables, and fluid hoses
- Empty inventory spots for small equipment, large equipment, and outfits
- Pulleys (only the fluid hose and electric cable variants)
- Manual control parts, including the torque crank and fluid pump (manual)
- A few sensors, including the gas meter, barometer, torque meter, laser sensor (missile)
- Several connectors, including the electric connector, fluid connector, torque connector, small connector, and all three hardpoint types.
- 'Anchors', including the rope anchor, fluid hose anchor, and electric cable anchor
- Wheels, but only the 3x3 wheel and the wheel coaster
- [Ladders](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Ladder)
- [Handles](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Handle)
- Basic logic blocks ('and', 'or', 'not', constant on, constant number)
- Small turret ring
- Friction pad
- Flags (small/medium/large)
- RX Directional and RX Directional (Large), long-range directional radios useful for communicating with spacecraft in orbit.

## Resource usage

Player vehicles can spawn with fuel automatically taken from the outpost's reserves. However, note that when a vehicle is despawned, any fuel it contains will not be automatically returned to the outpost. To keep the fuel, the vehicle must first be connected to the outpost's fuel supply stations with a fuel hose, and then the station must be set to pump the fuel back in. Ensure that the fuel hose is also disconnected and restocked on the pump before despawning the vehicle or it will be lost.

title: Gameplay/Gamemodes/Custom
summary:
Custom mode allows you to change world settings in-game, allowing you to adjust the weather, the time, teleport, use infinite electricity (or not) and so on. Unlike
Career
 mode, players will respawn after dying by default. It is analogous to Creative mode which preceded it. Under default settings, this mode does not have money, vehicles are free to spawn, all purchasable islands can be acquired for free (and even all acquired simultaneously through the menu). Players can also spawn or delete missions.

## Basic Physics

Stormworks contains a distinctive physics system

## Physics Of Mechanics

The Mechanic Physics of Stormworks follows a simplified version from real life, which the gravitational acceleration turns from g S E = 9.81 m s 2 {\textstyle g_{SE}={\frac {9.81m}{s^{2}}}} ![{\textstyle g_{SE}={\frac {9.81m}{s^{2}}}}](https://services.fandom.com/mathoid-facade/v1/media/math/render/svg/9c64173e70bfb4ea295932ce0a76e5566f95082c) to g S E = 10 m s 2 {\textstyle g_{SE}={\frac {10m}{s^{2}}}} ![{\textstyle g_{SE}={\frac {10m}{s^{2}}}}](https://services.fandom.com/mathoid-facade/v1/media/math/render/svg/6e3b6751696652a9356119be15f78275a2c59829)

### Constants

Stormworks Earth Gravitational acceleration: g S E = 10 m s 2 {\textstyle g_{SE}={\frac {10m}{s^{2}}}} ![{\textstyle g_{SE}={\frac {10m}{s^{2}}}}](https://services.fandom.com/mathoid-facade/v1/media/math/render/svg/6e3b6751696652a9356119be15f78275a2c59829) Stormworks Force unit: 1 n S = 1 k g 10 m s − 2 = 0.1 k g F {\textstyle 1n_{S}={\frac {1kg}{10ms^{-}2}}=0.1kgF} ![{\textstyle 1n_{S}={\frac {1kg}{10ms^{-}2}}=0.1kgF}](https://services.fandom.com/mathoid-facade/v1/media/math/render/svg/0abf756d46a275abebbe8a12f5c70e698f65b05c)

Momentum (Pivots/Hinges/Tracks):

- Mechanical parts like Pivots will produce an incredible amount of momentum. That means fast spinning velocity pivots will start to rotate your vehicle, even if the vehicle has a huge mass!

## Physics Of Fluid

The Fluid Physics of Stormworks follows a simplified physics which seems unrealistic due to its physics property.

### Pressure and Flow

The flow and the pressure of stormworks fluid is based on pressure gradient, which means the fluid in higher pressure tank or room are tend to move to lower pressure area

### Diffusion

Fluids are miscible between gases and liquids, which means they will balance the concentration when two rooms or tanks are connected(without single flow components, e.g., fluid flow valve, electric pumps), no matter the pressure and its gradient. However, relief valves can limit the fluid diffusion. When connecting two liquid storage spaces with a liquid relief valve, the diffusion will only occur for liquid but not gas, the same as the gas relief valve

### Liquid

Significantly, liquids in stormworks are not compressible

### Gas

## Aerodynamic

## RPS

## Physics Engine

Physics engine used: [Bullet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullet_(software))

The physics in this game tend to be worse than in other physics based games in alpha/beta/early access state [*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citation_needed)*]. Sometimes the behaviour of the engine is still not realistic (e.g. high forces of pivots turning the entire vehicle). The air drag in this game is much more than it is in real life, the air acts like a soup. Thus propellers and jets are more powerful. This also makes gliding difficult. Lift forces are barely noticable as the main force keeping flying objects up is their velocity.
