content.markdown:
**V1.5.9** of *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)* was released on August 26th, 2022.

## V1.5.9

- Feature - [#2486](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/2486) [#2712](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/2712) Manual pump, crank and valve
- Feature - [#8074](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/8074) Add keyboard binding support for vehicle editor
- Rework - [#12436](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/12436) Improved steam piston code for a smoother and more consistent behaviour
- Rework - [#12441](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/12441) Steam Piston now outputs the cam rotation instead of extension factor so stroke direction can be determined
- Rework - Starting weather state is now more heavily affected by world seed
- Fix - [#8934](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/8934) Fix tick delay consistency issue with Up/Down gate
- Fix - Players receiving healing when disconnecting from the server from a previously used medkit
- Fix - [#11620](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/11620) Fixed setVehiclePos not failing when passed nan values, adjusted processing for safe teleport (fix will only apply to new saves)
- Fix - [#11835](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/11835) Suspension labelling mistake
- Fix - [#11851](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/11851) Increased size of wheel colliders to better fit visually (old wheels sink into floor less)
- Fix - [#11993](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/11993) Seats not showing Trigger label if there is no labelled hotkey or axis
- Fix - [#12091](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/12091) Terminal Endo Hole in map
- Fix - [#12865](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/12865) Body armour double names
- Fix - [#12918](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/12918) Moved several non-sensor components out of the sensor category

## Source

- [Steam Community News](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/573090/view/3227412906480370153?l=english)

content.markdown:
**V1.6.11** of *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)* was released on January 26th, 2023.

## V1.6.11

- Feature - Multiplayer client physics optimization

- Fix - Several gameplay managers ticking their state while simulation is paused
- Fix - [#15336](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15336) Arid map colour discrepancies, added lua functions to support rock and gravel map colours
- Fix - [#14792](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14792) Default cargo container timer displaying negative values
- Rework - [#14626](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14626) Visually revised the mating surfaces for steam train parts to clarify that they need to be the same size and also oriented correctly to connect
- Balance - [#14967](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14967) Increased despawn times for processed metals dynamic objects
- Fix - [#14996](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14996) setTileInventory lua documentation
- Fix - [#15088](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15088) [#15570](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15570) Lua documentation content issues
- Fix - [#15210](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15210) Updated default resource storage vehicle
- Fix - [#15142](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15142) Updated missiles on default weapons AI destroyers
- Fix - [#15371](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15371) Default rescue scripts showing decimals for some numbers
- Fix - [#1554](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/1554) Re-exported Warner docks map tile geometry
- Fix - [#15655](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15655) Observatory landmark vehicle guard rail updates
- Fix - [#15683](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15683) Removed newlines from dog whistle description
- Fix - [#15688](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15688) Fixed block damage not parsing correctly (and optimized empty value parsing)
- Fix - Optimized trainline generation speed
- Fix - [#16044](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/16044) Updated desalinator description

A high volume of reports on the issue tracker have made us aware of a multiplayer issue regarding the old style wheel components. While we hope players are very happy with today's performance improvements we were unable to fix this issue for this release and hope to resolve it for a future update.

## Source

- [Steam Community News](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/573090/view/3629369950963350214?l=english)

- Fix - [#14595](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14595) Rope length output node now updates dynamically
- Fix - [#15169](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15169) Sync resource storage data on game join
- Fix - [#16146](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/16146) SpawnVehicleRope using the wrong data for loaded vehicles
- Fix - [#16288](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/16288) Respawn issues when respawning under delayed damage
- Fix - [#16404](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/16404) Ski mirroring issues
- Fix - [#16184](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/16184) Coal hopper network events for sub-bodies

- Added new sound effects for the Wildcat and [REDACTED]

Addon Lua:

- [#16090](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/16090) setVehiclePosSafe behavior reworked to avoid unreliable internal data

- [#3854](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/3854) Added setAudioMood which allows setting the audio mood to a higher level for a peer which naturally decreases over time

Added setAudioMood calls to the default missions script

- [#15918](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15918) Add support for map label type 0 to prevent crash

content.markdown:
**V1.6.14** of *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)* was released on February 17th, 2023.

## V1.6.14

- Feature - Physics Sensor ([#10065](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/10065) [#10119](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/10119) [#3793](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/3793) [#4465](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/4465))

The physics sensor component combines functionality of several other sensors into a convenient single block. The sensor outputs position, rotation, linear and angular speeds over 14 composite channels detailed on the component.

- Fix - [#16642](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/16642) Wheel secondary physics issues for clients
- Fix - [#17831](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/17831) Seafloor generation issue
- Fix - [#15856](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15856) No longer convert rescued survivors to static NPCs, instead update their display name to 'Rescued'
- Fix - [#13931](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/13931) Ai boats/aircraft now track damage and despawn after 2 mins if above threshold
- Fix - [#13936](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/13936) Return value of getZones not including Zone parent vehicle data
- Fix - [#14017](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14017) Added editor arrows for wings
- Fix - [#14835](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14835) Fixed teleporting under the map through very tall terrain

content.markdown:
**V1.6.2** of *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)* was released on October 13th, 2022.

## V1.6.2

Features marked with [DLC] are only available via the new Industrial Frontier DLC. Due to reworks to the trainlines, game mechanics and default playlists we strongly encourage users to create new saves for this update.

## Features

- Feature - Sawyer Isle Trainlines

Revamped the railways on the Sawyer isles with scenic coastal cliff and valley routes, rail-road crossings and a new large train depot. The outbound connection has been relocated from the north to the west coast of the island, with a new route to the south which connects to the New Arid biome if the DLC is enabled.

- Feature - Mining and Refining

New Mineral Drill vehicle component for mining coal and ore from the ground.

Updated the Dean Hall (Sawyer) and Old Arnold (Donkk) quarries with coal deposits. Updated the Underwater caves with uranium ore deposits. Coal gantries at the quarries have been removed.

Renamed coal ducts/funnels/hoppers to mineral ducts/funnels/hoppers and added mineral type filters.

Uranium ore can be refined into Ingots at the XFury Drilling Co. in the arctic.

- Feature - Workbench resource storage

Tiles now have an internal inventory for Diesel, Jet Fuel, Coal and Uranium Ingots. Information for tile inventories can be viewed on the fast travel tooltip for a base or within the workbench itself by expanding the currency button in the bottom right of the editor.

The Auto-refuel setting has been removed: Instead of filling inventories with fuel using money the resources are directly consumed from the workbench's inventory.

A new default addon 'default_resource_storage' has been created to supersede 'default_fuel_stores': Jet fuel and Diesel can be pumped out through the provided pumps, Coal and Uranium Ingots can be deposited via the hopper.

Uranium Ingots are now required to fuel nuclear fuel rods.

- [DLC] Feature - Arid Mega Island

A vast 300 Square Kilometer territory featuring Salt Flats, Mesa Desert, Rocky Mountains and a Huge Volcano. A mix of truck stops and isolated industrial facilities are scattered throughout with an emphasis on truck and train logistics. Deliver ores to the foundry via rail or explore the abandoned nuclear facility (Bringing a hazmat suit is advised).

When the DLC is enabled the preset starting tiles (Beginner Outpost / Creative Island) will be replaced with their Arid island counterparts.

- [DLC] Feature - Animals and Stormwoofs

Animals now spawn throughout the world of stormworks. Chase the seals in the arctic or race wild horses on the salt flats but watch out for bears in the woods.

Stormwoofs (Dogs) are a rare spawn that can appear near bases or residential areas in the world. Unlike other animals they can be issued commands with the new Dog Whistle component to assist you on search and rescue operations. Stormwoofs will alert players to nearby survivors by barking in their direction. There is a guaranteed spawn location at the North Meier Outpost and FJ Warner Docks.

Yes, you can pet the dogs! (and many other animals)

Additionally we have added a 'Bear Attack' mission complication for thematic rescue mission types

- [DLC] Feature - Metals and Metal Ore

The Arid Biome is formed from mineral dense rock and is home to several quarries and mines, with gold ores scattered across the plateaus beneath the surface sand.

Players will find Iron, Aluminium, Uranium and Gold Dirt deposits, which require processing at specialist facilities scattered across the islands.

- - Gold Dirt can be sifted for Gold Ore at the Ace Master Separator.
- - Refine Uranium Ore at the Uran Wind Power Plant.
- - Smelt Iron and Aluminium and Gold Ores into ingots or temper Iron Ingots with Coal to make Steel at the Empire Industries Foundry
- - Purify Dirty Gold Ingots into Pure Gold Bars at the Mallamar Mineral Lab

## Fixes

Changes that include a #NUMBER relate to fixes or features submitted by the Stormworks community via geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks which can be accessed via the 'Report Bug/Request Feature' button in-game.

Posting a submission to this tracker ensures we review your suggestion/report since we may not see reports submitted via other channels.

- Revert - Reverted a fix to damage parsing that was causing highly increased load times for vehicle states
- Fix - Crash caused by new train wheel assembly 3x particles
- Fix - Improved client catchup when under high render load
- Fix - #13755 Adjusted physics triangle culling (holes in floor)
- Fix - Birds maximum flight height increased
- Fix - #13641 Rail junction tile with incorrect connection flag
- Rework - Tile generation reworked; seeds should persist in future versions
- Rework - Coal (and Minerals) ground despawn time increased to 60sec
- Rework - Coal (and Minerals) now sink in water
- Rework - Updated mineral duct component network events for better sync
- Rework - Mission characters no longer apply their orientation (Fix NPCs facing away from player)
- Rework - 'First time' new game auto-setup now disables DLC

## Misc Changes

Added links to DLC store pages on the main menu if they are not owned.

Updated some dedicated server config names to reflect their in-game counterpart. These were added as aliases so old names will continue to work:

- aggressive_animals="true"
- sea_monsters="true"
- infinite_resources="true"

## Addon Lua

- Return false instead of error when dlc lua functions are called from non dlc save
- Fixed DLCWeapons script access error
- Fixed property.slider not displaying decimals
- Voxel-pos support for all set/get vehicle component functions
- get/setVehicleHopper can now set mineral inventory for all mineral holding components; and has an additional type parameter
- Added spawnVehicleRope
- Added getVehicleRopeHook
- Added getTileInventory
- Added setTileInventory
- Added dlcArid
- Added spawnCreature
- Added setCreatureMoveTarget

## Source

- [Steam Community News](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/573090/view/3316362713287482366)

content.markdown:
**V1.6.3-5** of *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)* was released on October 25th, 2022.

## V1.6.3-5

Halloween Seasonal Event:

- Feature - Stormwoofs seasonal outfits
- Feature - Added several zombie creature types
- Feature - Aggressive creatures advanced AI
- Feature - Zombie Apocalypse Addon ([#5689](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/5689))
- Feature - Fluid tanks improved detailed tooltips
- Feature - Add Workbench for ground vehicles at North Meier Outpost ([#14888](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14888))

In this spooky update along with various bugfixes we have some new additions to our regular seasonal Halloween period:

Stormwoofs will temporarily have fun Halloween themed outfits on, with each breed having their own unique costume. (Let us know your favorite!)

Zombie Apocalypse mode is a new Addon which will be enabled over the Halloween period for players with both 'Search and Destroy' and 'Industrial Frontier' DLCs enabled. We recommend disabling the DLC weapons ai script as minimum when playing with this addon and if players wish to turn off this addon they can disable it as usual in the addon selector on the new game menu.

The zombies addon has various settings to balance the mode to your own preference, so make sure to check them out in the addon settings when creating a new world. With Default settings Stormworks will be plagued with undead lurking across the Sawyer and Arid biomes, with new aggressive creature advanced AI that respond to sounds like player footsteps or gunshots. Players can go guns blazing or opt for stealth and avoid zombie vision cones as they search buildings for randomly generated loot, breaking line of sight will cause the zombies to lose interest after a while. Loot (and zombies) will respawn after ~5 mins of a tile being unloaded, and random loot is themed to the location (Hospitals more likely to drop medical supplies etc).

Some of the following fixes are updates to default addon content or terrain, which may not be updated/fixed on pre-existing saves.

- Fix - [#14827](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14827) Updated default resource storage vehicle to fix an issue with pumping air after it runs out of fuel
- Fix - Repaired several trainline rail/mesh issues
- Fix - [#14938](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14938) Workbench not working at benzin gas station
- Fix - [#14989](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14989) 'Invisible walls' / for-sale sign physics not despawning correctly
- Fix - [#14866](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14866) Weapons outfits ids have now been corrected for inventory components
- Fix - [#10358](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/10358) Increased async network buffer size for vehicles
- Fix - [#13695](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/13695) Weather De-sync on load/join
- Fix - [#12053](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/12053) Winch audio persisting at max length
- Fix - [#13319](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/13319) Disabled some developer debug logs
- Fix - [#12318](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/12318) Fix syntax error in lua docs
- Fix - [#13911](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/13911) Oxygen tank and parachute animation issues
- Fix - [#14857](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14857) Unable to use scene ladders when carrying creature
- Fix - Tooltip not appearing on workbench when carrying creature

content.markdown:
**V1.6.8** of *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)* was released on November 25th, 2022.

## V1.6.8

- Feature - New sound effects and audio updates
- Feature - Addon editor component copy and paste support

In this minor update we are including some of the planned audio changes we have been developing;

- Engines and modular engines have new sounds with improved blending.
- Gearboxes now have a sound when changing ratio to give feedback to the player.
- Lightning/Thunder now have a selection of sounds based on the range of the storm.
- Marine propellers have new sounds with improved blending.
- Key buttons and circuit breakers have new sound effects.
- Throttle levers now make a button sound when pressed.
- Added a many new sound effects to the buzzer block (Sirens / Horns / Klaxons / Bells)

- Rework - [#11569](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/11569) Characters now only drop equipment on death instead of incapacitated
- Fix - [#15693](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15693) Common creature physics crash
- Fix - [#11619](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/11619) Removed some unnecessary surfaces from windows that prevented raycasts
- Fix - [#13348](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/13348) Winch up and down editor warnings inverted
- Fix - Lights sometimes rendering a light flare with 0 power
- Fix - [#13613](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/13613) Updated function block to handle very small values
- Fix - End effector no longer interacts with manual components
- Fix - Improved vehicle editor loading time
- Fix - [#3196](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/3196) Increase text length for detailed tooltip nodes
- Fix - [#14082](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14082) Army outfit mesh issues
- Fix - [#14088](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14088) Pilot Seat (Hotas) incorrect control display
- Fix - Fixed animal interactions when incapacitated in beds
- Fix - [#15075](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15075) Restored debug.log() behavior
- Fix - Creature sync inconsistencies
- Fix - Dogs fetching animation issue
- Rework - Removed minor healing from normal beds
- Rework - Static vehicles electric reworked, batteries on static vehicles have infinite charge, components on static vehicles no longer act as if they infinite electric

## Source

- [Steam Community News](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/573090/view/3531414035625603520?l=english)

summary:
V1.7.0
 of
Stormworks: Build and Rescue
 was released on March 16th, 2023.

content.markdown:
**V1.7.0** of *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)* was released on March 16th, 2023.

## V1.7.0

- Feature - Oil Industry Major Update

Oil drilling is a new late-game activity for Stormworks, with high start up costs but a large return on investment. Oil can be found under oil rig workbenches or under random ocean tiles (Purchase survey data from an oil company to reveal them on your map) Once you have located an area rich in oil it's time to set up an oil rig and start drilling!

Oil Survey:

- Randomly generated ocean oil deposits

- Oil Data Vendors which sell oil deposit location information

- Oil deposit below the static oil rig base

- 4 Oil Well locations on the [Meier Isles](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Arid_Island) ([Industrial Frontier DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Industrial_Frontier_DLC))

Attach a wellhead to the terrain above an oil deposit (These are pre-placed on the Meier Isles) Drill Rods can be fed into the top of this component with assistance from Drill Clamps and Connectors to pick up and join the rods. A rotary table and swivel provide rotation and slurry flow which are required for running the drill. Once the drill is spinning and has a supply of slurry, the rods need to be physically pushed into the wellhead to advance the drill. Drilling will saturate the slurry with mud and stone, which can be cleaned and recycled using a slurry filter and fresh water. After the drill arrives at the oil deposit, the oil can be extracted with a Pumpjack component paired directly to a swivel. The Pumpjack requires mechanical action to draw up the oil from the well.

Oil Drilling:

- Drill Rod Storage

- Drill Clamp

- Drill Connector

- Rotary Table

- Drill Swivel

- Wellhead

- Pumpjack

- New Fluids: Slurry and Saturated Slurry

- Slurry filter

Now that you have an excess of oil you don't just have to sell! Fractional Distillation is the process of separating crude oil into its more useful components. Heat up oil inside a contained volume to >300 degrees and use the distillation port to tap off diesel and jet-fuel fractions.

Fractional Distillation:

- Diesel Furnace

- Electric Furnace

- Distillation Port

- We have deprecated the fluid filter in this update for a much more simplified version of the component to emphasize the design challenge of fluid system building.
- When we deprecate parts they remain in the game files, and a replacement version is added; this means that your old vehicles will still work as usual, but the old version of the part will no longer appear in the edit inventory.

- General:

- New Fluid Filter

- Fix - [#1698](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/1698) Improved terrain at scxeech trading yard
- Rework - [#16315](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/16315) [#15892](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/15892) Resource trading addon now has surge pricing
- Rework - Temperature Sensor now uses compartment temperature if placed inside a sealed volume
- Rework - Radar now ignores moveable class objects
- Balance - Desalinator re-balance

- Addon Lua:

- Added getOilDeposits()

- Added large keypad support to setVehicleKeypad

## Source

- [Steam Community News](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/573090/view/3647388158746595952?l=english)

content.markdown:
**V1.7.5** of *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)* was released on May 12th, 2023.

## V1.7.5

- Feature - [#2429](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/2429) First Person Rope lengths

This update welcomes a new feature for ropes in Stormworks and also some behind the scenes changes to improve their behaviour.

First person rope items can now be cycled with the secondary action key to change their length: Dynamic(40m), 1m, 2m, 4m, 8m, 16m The Dynamic 40m behaviour represents the old auto-spooling behaviour where the length is set when attached to a second anchor. All other lengths represent new non-elastic lengths.

- - Ropes, hoses and cables are now less elastic and behave more consistently with high mass bodies.
- - Ropes, hoses and cables will now snap when their anchor is damaged.
- - Ropes will return to the default dynamic length when detached and picked up by a player.
- - Improved handling of ropes for unloading and loading vehicles.

- Fix - [#16738](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/16738) Animal biting characters releasing character physics partially underground
- Fix - [#16738](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/16738) Fix creatures being unplaceable in seats, correctly remove creatures from seats on death for clients
- Fix - Animals revived with defibrillator killing multiplayer clients with physics collision on bite
- Fix - Clients applying forces to carried creatures with kinematic physics
- Fix - Characters being incapacitated while already in ragdoll state from creature not syncing to multiplayer clients
- Fix - [#14119](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/14119) Rotate buttons not disappearing while in micro-controller menu
- Fix - [#17932](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/17932) Render moustaches under new hats
- Fix - [#17820](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/17820) Fixed safari male mesh
- Fix - Reactors now consider all fluid types when determining fluid volume to heat (prev. just water and seawater, leading to unexpected behaviour)
- Fix - C4 on vehicle twilight zone for clients
- Fix - Several uncommon physics crashes

Notes for Addon Lua:

- Due to the new ropes changes it is no longer possible to create ropes with a length less than the attach distance and this may affect some existing scripts using spawnVehicleRope.
- For distances less than 40m you should still be able to pass length 0 to automatically create a rope using the distance between anchors as the length.

content.markdown:
**V1.9.0** of *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)* was released on October 12th, 2023.

## V1.9.0

Space DLC Features:

- Feature - Atmosphere and Space Simulation
- Feature - Huge Moon Surface Playable Area
- Feature - Liquid Fuel Rockets
- Feature - Electrolyser Component
- Feature - RCS Thruster Component
- Feature - Reaction Wheel Component
- Feature - Astronomy Sensor Component
- Feature - Space Missions

General:

- Feature - World border wrapping
  - - The world of Stormworks now seamlessly warps you to the other side of the map when crossing an edge
  - - Updated the ambient temperature texture to reflect this change
- Feature - Large Solar Panels
- Feature - Fluid, Gas, Temperature and Pressure overhaul
  - - Fluids have been separated into liquids and gases
  - - New Gases: Oxygen, Carbon Dioxide(Exhaust), Nitrogen, Hydrogen
  - - Complete overhaul to fluid pressures, allowing gases to be compressed
  - - Complete overhaul to fluid transfer and exchange between components, including backflow and pressure levelling
  - - Compartments now have their own temperature and pressure data
  - - Player is now damaged from ambient pressure and heat in addition to height/proximity based damage
  - - Inventories now have a fluid port for recharging outfits with oxygen
  - - Fires now consume oxygen to burn and produce CO2
  - - Humans and animals now breathe which consumes Oxygen and generates CO2
  - - Ocean and atmospheric pressure now scales with altitude
  - - Rapid fluid exchange across door thresholds will now apply a force to objects in the flow
- Feature - Barometer Component
- Feature - Space/Backpack Seat
- Feature - 2 Space Suit Outfits
- Feature - Gravity calculation overhaul and improvements
  - - [DLC] Players can place vehicles into geostationary orbit at ~300km
  - - [DLC] Characters can float in space oriented by their camera direction
  - - Pseudo stable orbit gravity based on linear velocity (Explained below)
  - - Revised character falling pose
- Feature - Improved Jet/Rocket particle rendering
- Feature - New Rocket workbenches
- Feature - Vehicle Groups (sub-vehicle splitting)
  - - Vehicles with many 'sub-vehicles' are now split into completely separate vehicles on spawn
  - - Addon lua has been updated to reflect this change, which is detailed in the section below
- Feature - Improved the navigation of tile locations in the addon editor by splitting them by biome
- Feature - Photomode cinematic camera stabilization and increased tether range by x4
- Feature - Gas and liquid relief valve components
- Feature - Liquid and Gas meter components
- Feature - Gas Tanks
- Feature - Directional Radio components for long distance data exchange
- Feature - Solid propellant is now required to fuel SRBs, and can be refined with water and Aluminium
- Feature - Sound effects for pumps and other fluid components
- Feature - Added 30 Dollar Trainyard to the starting bases
- Fix - [#4846](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/4846) [#2798](https://geometa.co.uk/support/stormworks/2798) Fixed vehicle fires not contributing to ambient temperature
- Fix - Several particle effect rendering fixes
- Fix - Fixed issue with parented mission zones not despawning with their parent vehicle
- Fix - Dedicated server crash caused by clouds attempting to render
- Fix - Fixed composite read values for the modular engine cylinder air and fuel
- Fix - Fixed connection state sync for dock-door and nuclear parts
- Fix - Crash caused by saving while a tile was not thread loaded
- Fix - Flipping issues for components with no physics voxels
- Fix - Fixed flame/jets rendering stutters
- Fix - Internal RX signal strength integer overflow errors
- Fix - Default missions not updating parented delivery zones transforms
- Fix - Several multiplayer improvements to address nearby vehicle desync and frequency
- Fix - Improved client character grounded vehicle detection
- Rework - Removed sunrise/sunset slider in place of separate Day/Night duration sliders
- Rework - Rescaled rewards for tow missions

Addon Lua:

- GetVehicleData - added group_id, removed filename
- GetVehicleGroup
- DespawnVehicleGroup
- SetGroupPos
- SetGroupPosSafe
- OnGroupSpawn
- SpawnAddonComponent - split id data - object_id, group_id, vehicle_ids[]

- GetTileInventory and setTileInventory now support propellant

- GetAstroPos

Dev Notes and Tips:

- Tip - Be careful when opening doors between differently pressurized areas...you may find yourself flung out into space!
- Tip - DLC owners get the new Stormworks theme space remix as the default main menu music
- Tip - Many earthly positional data components don't work in space, make sure you are prepared to navigate manually or with an astronomy sensor
- Tip - Components that rely on air/oxygen will be much less effective at higher altitudes as the atmosphere thins
- Tip - Characters and creatures need oxygen to breathe, don't trap yourself in a small box with no ventilation
- Tip - The fire extinguisher can be used to propel yourself in space!

## Source

- [Steam Community News](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/573090/view/6563491834170521765?l=english)

**V1.9.12** of *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)* was released on November 1st, 2023.

## V1.9.12

- Fix - fixed dedicated server crash
- Fix - fixed jet engines with inf fuel
- Fix - limit fluid transfer through doors based on compartment size to resolve oscillating with very small compartments
- Rework - liquid fuel engine internal capacity now based on engine size to improve flow
- Rework - premade engine internal capacity now based on engine size to improve flow
- Rework - increased modular engine fuel manifold capacity to improve fuel flow at low pressures
- Rework - water jets now convert momentum less agressively to reduce power stall
- Rework - reduced backflow threshold so that backflow only occurs with low or zero flow (improves pressure inside leaking compartments)
- Rework - rebalanced diesel burner to heat up slower
- Rework - reduced centrifugal separator internal capacity to make flow more responsive

title: Volcanic Chain
summary: The volcanic chain (located south west of the sawyer Islands) features an archipelago with a total of 21 landmasses (13 of which are realistically usable), they are also arranged much like the Hawaiian Islands.

content.markdown:
## Geography (Location)

The volcanic chain (located south west of the sawyer Islands) features an archipelago with a total of 21 landmasses (13 of which are realistically usable), they are also arranged much like the Hawaiian Islands.

## Underwater Features

The Islands also have unique underwater features, which include, but are not limited to:

- Underwater "hills"

- Four unique underwater sites (Killmans Scuttle, Natarera Ruins, Andzen Trench and the Lair of Mobius)

- Immense network of complex underwater caves (Lair of Mobius). At the indicated map coordinates, the cave can be directly entered and explored by a diver or submarine. There are also three islands which have cave entrances on land. The caves contain uranium ore deposits, necessary for getting the fuel to spawn vehicles which use [nuclear power](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Nuclear_power) in [career](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Gamemodes/Career) or [classic](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Gamemodes/Classic).

## Surface Features

Most of the Islands present in the archipelago have active volcanos on them, adding to the unique atmosphere.

The archipelago Includes 10 named Islands, Including: (From left to right by location)

- G Tugg Peak

- Cod Cape

- Sid V Point

- Mount Gerunimo

- Mount Spider

- Mount Murtak

- Rootin Tootin Rock

- Mount Trapdoor

- Mount GB Danny

+ Main Landmass

## Locations

The Volcanic Chain includes 3 main surface locations, including:

- **EggNog Cave**. The cave itself is underwater, but the entrance is accessed on the surface around the middle of the northern side of the island. There is a short, narrow, somewhat uneven path from the beach into the mouth of the cave. Connects to the Lair of Mobius cave system as discussed above.

- **Lorgs Cove**. There is an underwater cave near the center of the island which is accessed from the surface. Connects to the Lair of Mobius cave system as discussed above. The northeastern beach provides a flat, wide open space for moving a submersible over land to enter the cave. [Loot chests](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Loot_crate) may be found near the entrance to the cave.

- **Cavern of Thales** There is an underwater cave accessed from the surface. The cave entrance is at the southeastern side of the island and faces east. Connects to the Lair of Mobius cave system as discussed above. There is a large beach providing a relatively flat route for moving submersibles into the cave. Loot chests may be found near the entrance to the cave.

content.markdown:
## Structure

Volcanoes are large geological formations that can be found in multiple areas around the map, always appearing in the same place no matter the world's seed. They resemble large mountains, except with a crater at the peak that is permanently filled with glowing lava, and out of which rise large clouds of smoke. Being near said lava will heat the player, and jumping in it will burn the player, quickly killing them. The lava will also damage vehicles' parts that come into contact with it, and set them on fire. The volcano's slopes are covered in lava flows, which appear as a darker section of rock during normal conditions.

## Eruption

[![Mount Goldblum during the early stages of an eruption. Note the pyroclastic flow, debris, and glowing lava flow.](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/6/6a/MtGoldblum_Eruption.png/revision/latest?cb=20230626220435)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:MtGoldblum_Eruption.png](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:MtGoldblum_Eruption.png)

Mount Goldblum during the early stages of an eruption. Note the pyroclastic flow, debris, and glowing lava flow.

Eruption events can occur naturally or be caused by a player forcing one through the custom menu. Their start is signaled by an earthquake, which causes the camera to shake. It does not appear to influence vehicles nearby at this stage. The shaking will intensify, before numerous explosions can be seen at the peak of the volcano. These explosions will damage vehicles in the vicinity of the volcano.

A [pyroclastic flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyroclastic_flow) will be seen descending from the peak along the slopes, and chunks of rock will be propelled from the volcano at very high speeds. exploding and starting forest fires when they hit the ground. It is at this time that the lava flows on the volcano's slopes will start to glow orange, like the lava in the crater, and will have the same effects. A very large area of the map centered around the volcano will become clouded in grey ash, restricting visibility.

After the earthquake first starts, the player has about ten seconds to seek shelter before the explosions at the peak commence. The shaking will continue for roughly sixty seconds, before dying down, but will become stronger if the player is near a pyroclastic flow. The pyroclastic flows will damage players outside vehicles and greatly reduce visibility to those inside vehicles. The explosive rocks will cease at the same time as the earthquake, but the ash will stay in the air for a while longer. The main danger at this point is the difficulty to see because of the ash, and the forest fires that could have been started by falling debris.

## Locations

There are eight volcanoes total throughout the map of Stormworks, all of varying sizes. Most of them are situated in the volcanic island chain to the west of the map, but some can be found elsewhere. They are:

[![The volcanic island chain, seen from the sea](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/7/78/Volcanic_Islands.png/revision/latest?cb=20230626220436)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Volcanic_Islands.png](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Volcanic_Islands.png)

The volcanic island chain, seen from the sea

- Mount Paradize, located in the south-west quarter of the [Arctic](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Arctic)
- Mount Goldblum, located in the center of the [Sawyer Islands](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Sawyer_Islands)
- Biba Volcano, located in the south-east of the [Arid Island](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Arid_Island)
- Mount GB Danny, part of the volcanic island chain
- Mount Trapdoor, part of the volcanic island chain
- Mount Murtak, part of the volcanic island chain
- Mount Gerunimo, part of the volcanic island chain
- Sid V Point, part of the volcanic island chain

All of these volcanoes can undergo eruption events, with those in the volcanic chain becoming active if one of them erupts.

## Tips

- If you know a volcano will erupt soon, it is generally a good idea to avoid approaching it. Keep in mind that the extreme weather warning will display on the map quite a while before the volcano will actually erupt.
- If you must approach a volcano, do not get too close when it explodes as this can damage your vehicle and harm you.
- If you are near a volcano during an eruption and survive the initial explosions, it is recommended to try and get away as quickly as possible to avoid being struck by falling debris. Do so inside of a sealed vehicle, as the pyroclastic flows only hurt players outside of vehicles.
- Volcanic eruptions often start forest fires nearby, which will appear on the map once the eruption stops. It may be a good idea to fill water tanks on your firefighting vehicle ahead of time to be able to respond to these forest fires quickly.

## Trivia

- The volcanoes appear to be named after prominent Stormworks players, two examples being Mount Murtak being named after [Sir Murtak](https://steamcommunity.com/id/Sir_Murtak/myworkshopfiles/?appid=573090) and mount Gerunimo being named after [GERUNIMO](https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198024374919/myworkshopfiles/?appid=573090).
- Mount Spider appears to be a dormant volcano, with a crater and lava flows, but without lava. It will never erupt, even when using the custom menu.

Structure

Volcanoes are large geological formations that can be found in multiple areas around the map, always appearing in the same place no matter the world's seed. They resemble large mountains, except with a crater at the peak that is permanently filled with glowing lava, and out of which rise large clouds of smoke. Being near said lava will heat the player, and jumping in it will burn the player, quickly killing them. The lava will also damage vehicles' parts that come into contact with it, and set them on fire. The volcano's slopes are covered in lava flows, which appear as a darker section of rock during normal conditions.

Eruption

Mount Goldblum during the early stages of an eruption. Note the pyroclastic flow, debris, and glowing lava flow.

Eruption events can occur naturally or be caused by a player forcing one through the
custom menu
. Their start is signaled by an earthquake, which causes the camera to shake. It does not appear to influence vehicles nearby at this stage. The shaking will intensify, before numerous explosions can be seen at the peak of the volcano. These explosions will damage vehicles in the vicinity of the volcano.

A
pyroclastic flow
 will be seen descending from the peak along the slopes, and chunks of rock will be propelled from the volcano at very high speeds. exploding and starting
forest fires
 when they hit the ground. It is at this time that the lava flows on the volcano's slopes will start to glow orange, like the lava in the crater, and will have the same effects. A very large area of the map centered around the volcano will become clouded in grey ash, restricting visibility.

After the earthquake first starts, the player has about ten seconds to seek shelter before the explosions at the peak commence. The shaking will continue for roughly sixty seconds, before dying down, but will become stronger if the player is near a pyroclastic flow. The pyroclastic flows will damage players outside vehicles and greatly reduce visibility to those inside vehicles. The explosive rocks will cease at the same time as the earthquake, but the ash will stay in the air for a while longer. The main danger at this point is the difficulty to see because of the ash, and the forest fires that could have been started by falling debris.

Locations

There are eight volcanoes total throughout the map of Stormworks, all of varying sizes. Most of them are situated in the volcanic island chain to the west of the map, but some can be found elsewhere. They are:

The volcanic island chain, seen from the sea

Mount Paradize, located in the south-west quarter of the
Arctic

Mount Goldblum, located in the center of the
Sawyer Islands

Biba Volcano, located in the south-east of the
Arid Island

Mount GB Danny, part of the volcanic island chain

Mount Trapdoor, part of the volcanic island chain

Mount Murtak, part of the volcanic island chain

Mount Gerunimo, part of the volcanic island chain

Sid V Point, part of the volcanic island chain

All of these volcanoes can undergo eruption events, with those in the volcanic chain becoming active if one of them erupts.

Tips

If you know a volcano will erupt soon, it is generally a good idea to avoid approaching it. Keep in mind that the
extreme weather warning
 will display on the map quite a while before the volcano will actually erupt.

If you must approach a volcano, do not get too close when it explodes as this can damage your vehicle and harm you.

If you are near a volcano during an eruption and survive the initial explosions, it is recommended to try and get away as quickly as possible to avoid being struck by falling debris. Do so inside of a sealed vehicle, as the pyroclastic flows only hurt players outside of vehicles.

Volcanic eruptions often start forest fires nearby, which will appear on the map once the eruption stops. It may be a good idea to fill water tanks on your firefighting vehicle ahead of time to be able to respond to these forest fires quickly.

Trivia

The volcanoes appear to be named after prominent Stormworks players, two examples being Mount Murtak being named after
Sir Murtak
 and mount Gerunimo being named after
GERUNIMO
.

Mount Spider appears to be a dormant volcano, with a crater and lava flows, but without lava. It will never erupt, even when using the
custom menu
.

## Airplanes

Airplanes generate lift by using [wings](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Vehicle_Control#Wing_Front_Section). More information on [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lift_(force)).

You need to place the wings like this to create lift: [![Wing Lift](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/d/d0/Wing_Lift.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/150?cb=20190514095316)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/d/d0/Wing_Lift.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20190514095316)

1. Learn about [control surfaces of airplanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_control_surfaces). 2. Choose a propulsion system: Propellers (powered by aircraft engines) for small and medium speed or jet engines for high speed

3. Always use a PID to control jet engines

4. Have a look at Aircraft and Helicopter Standards

## Dedicated Server

Choose the guide depending on

- your setup (pc with screen / server without screen / command line only)
- your prefered installation method (manual / automatic)

## Pro's and Con's

**Automatic (SteamCMD & condenser)**

+ works with command line access (no screen or Remote Desktop Connection) + Install server in < 5 minutes + 4 scripts included (install, update, start, stop) + uses steamcmd (does not affect the normal steam client, does not need a steam account) - security settings are being changed to allow the powershell scripts to run - fixed installation path ("C:/steacmd" and "C:/condenser")

**Manual (SteamCMD)**

+ works with command line access (no screen or Remote Desktop Connection) + uses steamcmd (does not affect the normal steam client, does not need a steam account) + you have full control over the installation process - you must install SteamCMD manually - you must install/update/start/stop the Stormworks Dedicated Server manually

**Manual (Normal Steam Client)**

+ automatic installation and updates by Steam - you must start/stop the Stormworks Dedicated Server manually - does affect the normal steam client (it shows you playing Stormworks Dedicated Server, ...)

## Automatic (Official SteamCMD & condenser)

Follow this manual (written by me, CrazyFluffyPony): [https://gitlab.com/stormworks-tools/dedicated-server-install-script/-/blob/master/README.md](https://gitlab.com/stormworks-tools/dedicated-server-install-script/-/blob/master/README.md)

## Manual (Official SteamCMD)

Follow this manual (written by Beginner): [https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1995371855](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1995371855)

## Manual (Normal Steam Client)

- Install Steam Client and login
- in your bibliothecary search for "Stormworks" and enable the filter "Tools"
- you should see the "Stormworks Dedicated Server" Tool
- install it
- after installation you can go to the installation folder (right click the game -> properties -> location on disk)
- now you can follow Beginner's guide on steam, start at the section "Server Configuration"
- [https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1995371855](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1995371855)

## Rentable Stormworks servers

List of gameserver providers (GSPs) with Stormworks preinstalled and configured:

- LOW.MS: [https://low.ms/game-servers/stormworks-build-and-rescue-server-hosting](https://low.ms/game-servers/stormworks-build-and-rescue-server-hosting)
- ZAP-Hosting: [https://zap-hosting.com/en/stormworks-server-hosting/](https://zap-hosting.com/en/stormworks-server-hosting/)

## Engine

[![Engine Description](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/2/29/Engine_Description.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20190217210136)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/2/29/Engine_Description.png/revision/latest?cb=20190217210136)

The term engine describes any object which provides [mechanical power](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Game_Mechanics/Mechanical_Power) when provided with [fuel](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Game_Mechanics/Fuel), and something to burn fuel with, like air or oxygen. As well as fluid to cool the engine.

This article looks at the Engine component, a small diesel engine (not to be confused with the [Diesel Engine](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Propulsion) also known as the *large* diesel engine).

The small diesel engine provides mechanical power to other components. It accepts a throttle input, allowing the output of the engine to be controlled. It is often the first component placed on any design after basic blocks.

It is commonly paired with a [Wiki/Guides/Gearbox](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Guides/Gearbox) and [clutch](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Propulsion) to provide a full drivetrain. It is possible for the engine to overheat, so it requires a coolant (typically [water](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Game_Mechanics/Fluids)) to be pumped in and out of the engine (which is supported by the engine's own suction). The engine requires an in-take of air, and it also requires [diesel fuel](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Game_Mechanics/Fuel) to operate. Finally, an [exhaust](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Fluids) is required to pump out the fumes created from the engine's operation.

Add/Connect a battery, then using logic connect the electricity where required. Put down an electric circuit breaker if you want to toggle the electric engine or just add an electric motor and use pipes to connect it to what you are powering. go to logic and connect the desired controls to the electric motor(What drives the vehicle) and controls for the modular engine(What generates electricity).

if you want an engine that is using both motors to power the car, connect both motors to what you are powering

## Fluid Cannon

[![Fluid Cannon](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/e/e9/Fluid_Cannon.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20190211194153)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/e/e9/Fluid_Cannon.png/revision/latest?cb=20190211194153)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Fluid_Cannon.png](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Fluid_Cannon.png)

Fluid Cannon

[![Active Water Cannon](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/a/a9/Water_cannon_in_use.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/197?cb=20190211201204)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/a/a9/Water_cannon_in_use.png/revision/latest?cb=20190211201204)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Water_cannon_in_use.png](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Water_cannon_in_use.png)

Active Water Cannon

The Fluid Cannon is a component available in [normal mode](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Normal_Mode) and [advanced mode](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Advanced_Mode) that is primarily used for creating a turret to put out fires. It normally is attached to a [Fluid Tank](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Fluids) with a [Fluid Pump](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Fluids) to provide pressure.

### Requirements

The Fluid Cannon needs a pressurised fluid supply, invariably water. In Advanced mode, it also requires an electricity supply. The turret's direction can be controlled using logic data inputs, such as throttles.

## Example Normal Mode Water Cannon

[![A functioning water cannon](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/d/df/Water_cannon_example.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/253?cb=20190211195426)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/d/df/Water_cannon_example.png/revision/latest?cb=20190211195426)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Water_cannon_example.png](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Water_cannon_example.png)

A functioning water cannon

An example configuration for a water cannon compromising of a [Fluid Tank Large](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Fluids), a [Large Fluid Pump](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Fluids), a Fluid Cannon, a [Toggle Button](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/User_Input), two [Throttle](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/User_Input)s, and (optionally) a [numeric inverter](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Logic). Note that since we are not in Advanced mode, the fluid connections do not need to line up directly with pipes and thus the components can be placed anywhere on the ship. The only thing that matters is they are connected via Logic connections.

- The Fluid Tank Large provides the source of water. Naturally there are other ways of getting water out at sea, but this is good enough for us. Note that the Fluid Tank Large **must** be set to the Water type using the 'Select' tool.
- The Large Fluid Pump takes the water from the Fluid Tank Large and pressurises it, which prepares the water for being fired out of the cannon.
- The Fluid Cannon takes the water from the Large Fluid Pump and fires it out of the turret at the fire (or perhaps another target).
- The Toggle Button is attached to the Large Fluid Pump on the Logic Data screen, allowing the pump to be turned on and off. This allows the operator to control when the cannon is in use or not.
- The Throttles are used to move the turret left/right and up/down. They should be selected with the Select tool and their Min Value set to -1 rather than 0. This allows them to move in both directions. A numeric inverter can be also be added as a connection between the throttles and the fluid cannons to reverse any connections which seem 'backwards'.

### Logic Connections

[![Water Cannon Fluid Connections](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/5/5f/Water_Cannon_Fluid_Connections.png/revision/latest?cb=20190211201049)

[![Water Cannon Data Connections](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/e/e9/Water_Cannon_Data_Connections.png/revision/latest?cb=20190211200551)

- The Toggle Button should have a Data connection to the Large Fluid Pump
- The Throttles should have a Data connection to the Fluid Cannon's two axes, one each.
- If a Throttle is the wrong way around, a Numeric Inverter should be added. The Throttle should then be connected to the Numeric Inverter first, with the Numeric Inverter then connected to the appropriate Fluid Cannon node. You may need two. Or you could just turn the throttles around, but where's the fun in that?
- The Fluid Tank Large's Fluid Out node should be connected to the Large Fluid Pump's Fluid In node.
- The Large Fluid Pump's Fluid Out node should be connected to the Fluid Cannon's Fluid In node.

### Additional Ideas

The power of the pump can be altered to give less pressure with the Select tool. This can be really helpful, as the cannon will spray more widely instead of firing a long distance in a tight formation.

Try strapping a Fluid Cannon to a [linear track base](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Mechanics) for a nippy turret right where you need it.

Turrets are cool, but fire [hoses](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Fluids) can be more flexible.

## Fluids

**Fluid** is a mechanism in Stormworks based on enclosed space and pipelines. This game's **Fluid** system allows you to realize many functions like transferring fuel, air, or cooling down your vehicle.

Here are some video guides on fluid:

## Fluid Mechanism

The fluid system of this game is complex, which includes pressure, heat, and many types of fluids.

Liquids and gases are both used in the fluid system. In an enclosed space (e.g. a custom fluid container), liquid will visibly appear to stay at the bottom while gas will stay at the top. However, fluid ports drawing fluid from the space will take both liquid and gas, regardless of their location in the tank. For example, a fluid port to drain the bottom of a mostly full ballast tank will still take both air and water when it is drained.

Similar to the real world, liquids are incompressible, while gases are compressible (up to a limit of 60 atm, where they also become incompressible).

### Liquid

#### Water

There are two types of water in this game: **Fresh Water** and **Sea Water** Fresh Water can be generated in a workspace by using a fluid spawner, or can be slowly produced in a mobile fashion by converting by sea water using desalinators.

#### Fuel

There are two types of liquid [fuel](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Mechanics/Fuel) in this game: diesel and jet fuel.

#### Other

**Crude oil** Crude oil can't be spawned with a fluid spawner, but can be extracted with an oil rig or collected from the sea surface when cleaning up an oil spill.

**Slurry** Slurry is used to help with drilling for oil.

### Gas

#### Air

There are 3 types of gas that naturally exist in the air: **Nitrogen**,**Oxygen** and **Carbon Dioxide**.

Suffocation occurs in only 2 situations: when carbon dioxide concentration > 10% or oxygen concentration < 15%, upon which the blue bar for holding breath is shown.

#### Steam

Steam can be generated by boiling fresh water in a boiler at more than 100 Celcius.

#### Hydrogen

To generate and use hydrogen, you need the **Space DLC** Hydrogen can be extracted by hydrogen electrolyser and can be used as a rocket fuel.

### Pressure and Flow

The fluid flow is determined by pressure

### Diffusion

Fluid concentration and temperature is based on diffusion, which means they will automatically spread when two enclosed spaces or pipelines are connected. Diffusion occurs regardless of pressure, temperature or fluid type. For example, a tank of oxygen and a tank of carbon dioxide will mix if connected, even though fluid flow will show as 0.

Diffusion only occurs when 2 spaces or tanks are connected by fluid ports, pipelines, or doors. When pipelines have fluid flow valves or other components that limit the flow direction, diffusion is blocked and will not occur even though fluid would still flow between the two spaces with the help of a pressure gradient.

#### Concentration

#### Temperature

## Fluid Parts

### Pipe

Used to transfer mechanical power or fluid from A to B. Note that pipes will distribute both power and fluid if they are connected to both.

### [Pumps](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Pumps)

Used to pump fluid from A to B, make sure to have the **Fluid In** and **Fluid Out** ports situated correctly for normal flow direction

### Liquid and Gas Meter

You can use these to measure fluid in liters to find the capacity and current quantity of fluid in an enclosed space. Although liquid and gas meters will both meters show the same capacity for the same tank, they levels they show represent only the liquid and gas contents respectively.

### Fluid spawner

The **fluid spawner** is a part which you can use to generate fluid in an enclosed space. For 'Liquid', the volume of liquid spawned will occupy 99% of enclosed space when the fill level is set at 100%, the volume of liquid spawned can be calculated by **Enclosed Space** X **99%**(reserve space for air for 1 atm) X **fill level**

For **Gas**, The original air in the Enclosed Space will be removed and new gas will be spawned, the maximum pressure is 59.4 atm which is reached when the fill level is set to 100%.

## Tips

You can use fluid ports fluid-fluid heat exchangers instead of radiators and heat sinks just add pumps facing in the right orientation because the coolant pipes do not have suction when using fluid ports (engine suction will still work with radiators or heat sinks).

## See also

- [Gameplay/Mechanics/Fluids](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Mechanics/Fluids)
- [Pumps](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Pumps)

content.markdown:
## Gearbox

Gearboxes convert torque (rotational force) into rotational speed (rps) and the vice versa. They are extremely useful for optimizing engine performance and allowing vehicles to reverse direction. The degree of change depends on the ratio of the gearbox. A single gearbox in Stormworks can switch between two different ratios. There are currently 8 gearbox ratios to choose from: -1:1, 1:1, 6:5, 3:2, 9:5, 2:1, 5:2 and 3:1. For example, a ratio of 3:1 means that the outputted RPS or torque of the engine (depending on the direction of the gearbox) is multiplied by a factor of 3.

If the gearbox is facing the engine, as indicated by the blue arrows on the gearbox, RPS to the propeller will be multiplied at the expense of torque. An engine limited to 20 RPS would therefore spin an attached propeller with 60 RPS (given that there are no weight constraints that prevent the engine from reaching 20 RPS).

If the gearbox is facing away from the engine, the multiplication is applied with respect to torque. An engine outputting 40 torque, combined with a 3:1 gearbox, would deliver a resulting 120 torque. The increase in torque comes at the cost of RPS, which is divided by 3.

When building a vehicle, it is important to consider whether a high torque or RPS should be achieved. For example, trucks and tractors built to move heavy loads uphill would need gearboxes facing away from the engine which result in a large amount of torque, allowing it to pull heavy objects at low speed. In contrast, a sports car or helicopter would have gearboxes facing towards the engine, resulting in a low torque but higher RPS output and thus maximum speed. Note that because of the low torque, less force is needed to slow or stop the vehicle, so it could be even slower with towing a heavy load, or possibly fail to move at all.

The 1:-1 ratio is used to allow vehicles to run in reverse. In the current build, gearboxes have a 95% efficiency rating.

## Automatic transmission

For most air and sea vehicles, a single set of gears at fixed ratios is often good enough. However, ground vehicles must deal with change in slope, acceleration, and sometimes hauling very heavy loads. If the load is too heavy for the available torque, the engine can stall and stop working. If the load is too low and/or the vehicle moves downhill, the engine may run too fast, delivering less power than it could, using more fuel than necessary, and potentially risking overheating and bursting into flames. This makes an automatic transmission a near necessity for them. Cargo helicopters, tug boats, and cargo freighters often face similarly drastic changes in required torque and power and also benefit greatly from having an automatic transmission.

### Simple(r) approach

A relatively simple approach is to have four gearboxes, all 2:1, two facing the engine, two facing away. All should be configured to increase speed when off, so the gears facing the engine are 2:1 when off and 1:1 when on. The two facing away from the engine are 1:1 when off and 2:1 when on. Thus, each gearbox doubles torque and halves speed when turned on, allowing a range from 1:4 (improving torque) up to 4:1 (improving speed). The five possible configurations would be 1:4, 1:2, 1:1, 2:1, and 4:1. It doesn't matter which gearboxes are turned on, just that each added gearbox turned on will double torque at the expense of RPS.

To use these gearboxes, a microcontroller can be configured with an up/down counter which increments by 1 and is clamped to a range of 0-4. At 1, one of the gearboxes is turned on. At 2, two of them are turned on, and so on. A very simple method would be to use push buttons routed through a pulse, allowing the user to manually adjust the gears to double speed and halve torque, or vice versa, up through the full range of increments. A slightly more sophisticated method would be to check the RPS of the engine and automatically send such pulses to correct high or low rps (e.g. <6 rps, or >10 rps), resetting using RTO timers every half second or so (half a second to give the engine time to adjust after the gear change to see if further change is necessary) before sending additional pulses as necessary to keep the engine in the ideal range.

In testing, this approach works rather well, easily going up hills and over roads at excellent speed without excessive RPS, but the sharp transitions due to doubling and halving the torque / RPS make for somewhat 'jolty', lurching movement.

### Advanced approach

A more advanced approach is to use four different gear ratios to allow for a greater range of possible settings and therefore smoother transitions. For example, suppose gearbox A is 1:3, B is 5:9 (both facing away from the engine) C is 2:1 and D is 5:2 (both facing towards the engine), and all are 1:1 when off. Now we get maximum speed with just CD on, and maximum torque with just AB on.

These four gearboxes can be configured in 16 different ways to get gear ratios that were previously impossible. The options include AB 5:27 (=0.185), A 1:3 (=0.333), ABC 10:27 (0.370), ABD 25:54 (=0.463), B 5:9 (=0.556), AC 2:3 (=0.667), AD 5:6 (=0.833), ABCD 50:54 (=0.926), 1:1 (=1.00), BC 10:9 (=1.11), BD 25:18 (=1.39), ACD 5:3 (=1.67), C 2:1 (=2.00), D 5:2 (=2.50), BCD 25:9 (=2.78), CD 5:1 (=5.00). This approach gives us 35% more maximum torque, 25% more maximum speed, and most transitions between the gear settings are barely noticeable. Only the worst transitions (to the highest and lowest gear settings, respectively) remain 'jolty', but still only 90% as large as every transition used to be with the previous approach.

For this approach, we need the up/down counter to be clamped from 0 to 15. Transition times can also be much shorter e.g. 1/8th of a second, so if necessary we still do a full cycle of all gear combinations within two seconds as before.

A needs to be on for: 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11. B needs to be on for 0, 2, 3, 4, 7, 9, 10, 14. C needs to be on for 2, 5, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15. D needs to be on for 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15.

In testing, this approach works extremely well. The movement is smooth even while moving up and down slopes and the speed is higher than it was at previous throttle settings, requiring about 30% less throttle to avoid going too fast.

Gearbox

Gearboxes convert torque (rotational force) into rotational speed (rps) and the vice versa. They are extremely useful for optimizing engine performance and allowing vehicles to reverse direction. The degree of change depends on the ratio of the gearbox. A single gearbox in Stormworks can switch between two different ratios. There are currently 8 gearbox ratios to choose from: -1:1, 1:1, 6:5, 3:2, 9:5, 2:1, 5:2 and 3:1. For example, a ratio of 3:1 means that the outputted RPS or torque of the engine (depending on the direction of the gearbox) is multiplied by a factor of 3.

If the gearbox is facing the engine, as indicated by the blue arrows on the gearbox, RPS to the propeller will be multiplied at the expense of torque. An engine limited to 20 RPS would therefore spin an attached propeller with 60 RPS (given that there are no weight constraints that prevent the engine from reaching 20 RPS).

If the gearbox is facing away from the engine, the multiplication is applied with respect to torque. An engine outputting 40 torque, combined with a 3:1 gearbox, would deliver a resulting 120 torque. The increase in torque comes at the cost of RPS, which is divided by 3.

When building a vehicle, it is important to consider whether a high torque or RPS should be achieved. For example, trucks and tractors built to move heavy loads uphill would need gearboxes facing away from the engine which result in a large amount of torque, allowing it to pull heavy objects at low speed. In contrast, a sports car or helicopter would have gearboxes facing towards the engine, resulting in a low torque but higher RPS output and thus maximum speed. Note that because of the low torque, less force is needed to slow or stop the vehicle, so it could be even slower with towing a heavy load, or possibly fail to move at all.

The 1:-1 ratio is used to allow vehicles to run in reverse. In the current build, gearboxes have a 95% efficiency rating.

Automatic transmission

For most air and sea vehicles, a single set of gears at fixed ratios is often good enough. However, ground vehicles must deal with change in slope, acceleration, and sometimes hauling very heavy loads. If the load is too heavy for the available torque, the engine can stall and stop working. If the load is too low and/or the vehicle moves downhill, the engine may run too fast, delivering less power than it could, using more fuel than necessary, and potentially risking overheating and bursting into flames. This makes an automatic transmission a near necessity for them. Cargo helicopters, tug boats, and cargo freighters often face similarly drastic changes in required torque and power and also benefit greatly from having an automatic transmission.

Simple(r) approach

A relatively simple approach is to have four gearboxes, all 2:1, two facing the engine, two facing away. All should be configured to increase speed when off, so the gears facing the engine are 2:1 when off and 1:1 when on. The two facing away from the engine are 1:1 when off and 2:1 when on. Thus, each gearbox doubles torque and halves speed when turned on, allowing a range from 1:4 (improving torque) up to 4:1 (improving speed). The five possible configurations would be 1:4, 1:2, 1:1, 2:1, and 4:1. It doesn't matter which gearboxes are turned on, just that each added gearbox turned on will double torque at the expense of RPS.

To use these gearboxes, a microcontroller can be configured with an up/down counter which increments by 1 and is clamped to a range of 0-4. At 1, one of the gearboxes is turned on. At 2, two of them are turned on, and so on. A very simple method would be to use push buttons routed through a pulse, allowing the user to manually adjust the gears to double speed and halve torque, or vice versa, up through the full range of increments. A slightly more sophisticated method would be to check the RPS of the engine and automatically send such pulses to correct high or low rps (e.g. <6 rps, or >10 rps), resetting using RTO timers every half second or so (half a second to give the engine time to adjust after the gear change to see if further change is necessary) before sending additional pulses as necessary to keep the engine in the ideal range.

In testing, this approach works rather well, easily going up hills and over roads at excellent speed without excessive RPS, but the sharp transitions due to doubling and halving the torque / RPS make for somewhat 'jolty', lurching movement.

Advanced approach

A more advanced approach is to use four different gear ratios to allow for a greater range of possible settings and therefore smoother transitions. For example, suppose gearbox A is 1:3, B is 5:9 (both facing away from the engine) C is 2:1 and D is 5:2 (both facing towards the engine), and all are 1:1 when off. Now we get maximum speed with just CD on, and maximum torque with just AB on.

These four gearboxes can be configured in 16 different ways to get gear ratios that were previously impossible. The options include AB 5:27 (=0.185), A 1:3 (=0.333), ABC 10:27 (0.370), ABD 25:54 (=0.463), B 5:9 (=0.556), AC 2:3 (=0.667), AD 5:6 (=0.833), ABCD 50:54 (=0.926), 1:1 (=1.00), BC 10:9 (=1.11), BD 25:18 (=1.39), ACD 5:3 (=1.67), C 2:1 (=2.00), D 5:2 (=2.50), BCD 25:9 (=2.78), CD 5:1 (=5.00). This approach gives us 35% more maximum torque, 25% more maximum speed, and most transitions between the gear settings are barely noticeable. Only the worst transitions (to the highest and lowest gear settings, respectively) remain 'jolty', but still only 90% as large as every transition used to be with the previous approach.

For this approach, we need the up/down counter to be clamped from 0 to 15. Transition times can also be much shorter e.g. 1/8th of a second, so if necessary we still do a full cycle of all gear combinations within two seconds as before.

A needs to be on for: 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 11. B needs to be on for 0, 2, 3, 4, 7, 9, 10, 14. C needs to be on for 2, 5, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15. D needs to be on for 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15.

In testing, this approach works extremely well. The movement is smooth even while moving up and down slopes and the speed is higher than it was at previous throttle settings, requiring about 30% less throttle to avoid going too fast.

## Gyro

| Gyro |  |

| Mass | 10 |

| Logic inputs | Bool (Starter), Number (Throttle) |
| Logic outputs | Number (Temperature), Number (RPS) |
| Connections | Roll (In), Pitch (In), Yaw (In), Up/Down (In), Auto-hover (In), Stabilised Roll (Out), Stabilised Pitch (Out), Stabilised Yaw (Out), Stabilised Up/Down (Out) |
| Adjustable parameters | Min Throttle (0-100%), Max Throttle (0-100%), Roll (0-100%), Pitch (0-100%), Yaw (0-100%) |

Gyros take control inputs and translate them into output values that can be fed into [rotors](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Propulsion) for more controlled, stabilized flight. They can also be used for helping to keep a boat stabilized. The gyro component comes equipped with an auto-hover mode that attempts to prevent the vehicle from drifting when no inputs are being given, and which keeps the vehicle at a set pitch/roll when control inputs are used. The gyro also offers editable properties that allow for fine-tuning the sensitivity of the gyro's outputs on each individual axis.

## Integration

Gyros are most easily integrated into [helicopters](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Vehicles/Air/Helicopter) where the rotor component has inputs that correspond to the outputs of the gyro. The outputs of pilot seats can be fed directly into gyros easily and allow for stable controls that feel natural and intuitive.

On [boats](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Vehicles/Water/Boat), gyros can be used to control fins or rudders to maintain stable pitch and roll.
