'''Boats''' are one of the types of vehicle players can design and operate for their sea rescue service in ''[[Stormworks: Build and Rescue]]''.

This page was last updated for [[V1.5.1]] (18 July 2025).

== Overview of building a boat ==
[[File:Simple Boat Summary.png|thumb|A very simple boat design (19 blocks wide, 14 long, 5 high)]]
A minimal standard boat requires:

# [[Buoyancy]] provided by a closed area within the ship
# An engine to provide power
# A propeller to turn power in to thrust (i.e move the boat!)
# A rudder to permit steering left and right
# A pilot seat to allow the captain to start the engine, control the throttle, and to steer

Stormworks provides a starter boat and starter sailboat preset which can be loaded in the editor to save time, or you can continue reading to learn how to make your own from scratch.

== Buoyancy ==
{{Main|Buoyancy}}

The most important component of a typical boat is to ensure that it has a large enclosed area within the hull. This is typically below the main deck. It often contains the engine(s) for the vehicle. In overly simple terms, the amount of enclosed space in this area determines how much weight your boat can hold (its maximum ''displacement'') - meaning how much weight the ship can carry before it starts to sink. If there is a 'hole' in this part of the ship, the boat will usually immediately sink when spawned in-game because it cannot hold its own weight.

== [[Wiki/Guides/Engine|Engines]] ==
The simplest way to get a boat moving is with a built-in [[Wiki/Building/Components/Propulsion/DieselEngines|diesel engine]]. Pipes will be needed to connect fuel to the engine from fluid tanks; to connect the engine's exhaust to Fluid Exhaust pipes; to connect air from a fluid port or air filter to the engine's air intake; to connect the engine's power output to a propeller (possibly using a clutch and/or gearbox in between); and to connect coolant from the engine to a radiator or heat exchanger and back to the engine. The engine will also require [[electricity]] from a battery, a logic input to tell it when to run its starter, and a logic input for its throttle setting.

Note that engines tend to be quite heavy and can easily shift a boat's center of mass. It's recommended to keep engines as close to the bottom of the hull as possible to improve stability and to make it easier to flip back upright if does capsize.

== [[Wiki/Building/Components/Propulsion|Propellers]] ==
Engines by themselves generate power, but converting that power into forward (and backward) movement requires propellers.

Note that propellers lined up above the [[Wiki/Game Mechanics/Center of Mass|center of mass]] may pitch the ship down into the water (in extreme cases causing the ship to dive, choke the engine, and stop), while propellers far below the center of mass may pitch the ship up all the way out of the water (in extreme cases causing it to hop around almost uncontrollably over waves). Propellers slightly below the center of mass can help to tilt the boat upwards and lift it slightly out of the water, thereby reducing drag and increasing speed.

== Steering ==
[[File:Rudder data connection.png|right|frameless|484x484px]]
Boat steering can be done in a variety of ways. Rudders are among the easiest approach, though thrust pivoting, unequal propulsion, and lateral propulsion are all options as well.

=== Rudders ===
[[Wiki/Building/Components/Vehicle Control|Rudders]] allow the boat to turn by directing water to the sides of the boat as the boat moves forwards. This is their key limitation: they only work when the boat is moving forwards (or backwards). For boats that need to perform sharp turns or sometimes maneuver sideways, rudders are insufficient.

Normal rudders (not fin rudder) should be placed with the blocks at the top (on the underside of the boat) with the 'thin end' of the rudder pointing towards the back of the boat. In the Logic Data screen, rudders need to be connected to the A/D node of the pilot seat.

Rudders are often installed in a pair, with one at either side of the back of the boat (port and starboard). Note that if you use the symmetry tool when placing the rudders, they will counteract each other by trying to turn in opposite directions (as the symmetry tool flips them). They must be placed individually or else a separate logic arrangement to negate the turning instructions must be provided to one of the rudders.

=== Thrust pivoting ===
The built-in preset [[Starter Boat]] uses thrust pivoting. The engines at the back turn from one side to the other to steer the boat, causing their center of thrust to end up on different sides of the boat's [[center of mass]], resulting in a yawing force. Similarly, according to its description, the [[azimuth thruster]] is intended for use on a robotic pivot so that it can provide lateral thrust to allow a ship to move sideways or turn sharply. [[Fluid jet]]s can work similarly, using thrust deflectors to provide lateral force for turning.

=== Unequal propulsion ===
On a ship with at least two propellers, thrust on one propeller can be reduced, eliminated, or even reversed while the other propeller will both push the ship forward and turn it. With gearboxes or electric motors used to allow one propeller to reverse while the other goes forward, a ship can more or less turn on a dime.

=== Lateral propulsion ===
Some large real-life ships have side-oriented propellers to allow them to move sideways towards a dock. These can also be used for turning if they are offset from the center of mass.

== Pilot Seat ==
A control seat (often a [[Wiki/Building/Components/User Input|pilot seat]] or [[Wiki/Building/Components/User Input|helm]]) is the easiest way of setting up controls for a simple boat, although various [[Wiki/Building/Components/User Input|throttle]]s and buttons for control can be more satisfying.

A control seat, once placed, needs to be connected in the Logic Data screen to the components which it controls. W/S is usually used to control the throttle, while A/D is usually used to control the rudders, or power to lateral propellers.

Using the Select Tool, the pilot seat's Hotkey 1 can be set from 'push' to 'toggle' and used to control the on/off state of the engines. In the Logic Data screen, drag Hotkey 1 to the Engine On/Off node to connect it, then press '1' when in game to start the engines.

[[File:Hotkey set to toggle.png|frameless|682x682px]]

* Keep heavy parts low: The heaviest parts (engine, battery) should be placed on the bottom of the hull to keep the center of mass low.

* Add weights: If the center of mass is still too high, you can add weight blocks to the bottom of the ship. The lower these weights are, the more effective they will be. * Lights! Add [[Wiki/Building/Components/Lights|lights]] for when it gets dark, or you won't be able to see what's happening.
* Navigation tools! Add a [[compass sensor|compass]] so you can tell which way you are headed in career mode. Add a GPS so you can work out your position when it's dark or foggy and you can't see nearby islands.
* Fluid cannons! Add a [[Wiki/Guides/Fluid Cannon|fluid cannon]] to fire water from your ship, allowing you to put out fires.

== Alternative styles of boat ==

=== Catamaran ===
A catamaran is made up of two hulls which touch the water. They tend to be very stable, making them less likely to flip. On the other hand, when they do flip they are much harder to upright. Catamaran examples can be found on Wikipedia[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catamaran].

=== Hydrofoil ===
A hydrofoil is a type of high-speed boat which has control surfaces below the waterline. These surfaces are used to provide enough lift to get the boat entirely out of the water, resting only on the hydrofoils to minimize drag. Hydrofoil examples can be found on Wikipedia[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrofoil].

## Submersible

[![Example of a submersible](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/b/bb/Submersible_Example.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20190216000224)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/b/bb/Submersible_Example.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20190216000224)

[https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Submersible_Example.jpg](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/File:Submersible_Example.jpg)

Example of a submersible

**Submersibles** are one of the many types of vehicle players can design and operate for their sea rescue service in *[Stormworks: Build and Rescue](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormworks:_Build_and_Rescue)*.

Submersibles are similar to [boats](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Vehicles/Water/Boat), but have the ability to operate whilst fully underwater. By flooding the hull compartments, or 'ballasts' (sectioned-off areas of the vessel designed to be flooded and drained), a submersible can force itself to sink under the water. As with boats, [propellers](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Propulsion) are used for forward and backward motion, while [rudders](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Vehicle_Control) provide sideways movement, but are also used to provide upwards and downwards movement once underwater (known as 'hydroplanes'). An auto-ballast mechanism is often used to achieve neutral [bouyancy](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Game_Mechanics/Bouyancy) by filling fore and aft ballasts according to the submersible's required weight distribution, making controlling the submersible much easier. A submarine often benefits greatly from having a very low center of mass as they do not need to stay above the water during manoeuvres, and have a tendency to roll.

### Power Sources

In [Advanced Mode](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Advanced_Mode), a submersible is typically powered underwater by [batteries](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Electricity), using diesel [engines](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Guides/Engine) only on the surface to charge the batteries (this setup is known as 'diesel-electric'). In [Normal Mode](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Normal_Mode), batteries are not available, so diesel engines are typically used instead. In the [V1.2.1](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V1.2.1) update, nuclear power sources were added to *Stormworks*. This new form of [fuel](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Game_Mechanics/Fuel) allows players to utilise nuclear energy to power submersibles. Unlike engines, nuclear power generation is a process which does not need access to air.

## Ballasts

In a typical submersible design, the lower third (or even half) of the vessel is reserved for ballast. Unlike on a [boat](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Vehicles/Water/Boat) where these compartments would be left as air and closed off entirely, they are flooded to allow the submersible to sink. To do this, [Fluid Pumps](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Fluids) are used to push water in and out of the compartment through [Fluid Ports](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Fluids) that separate the inside of the ballast tank from the sea (or air).

Typically there are two ballasts, one in the fore (front) and one in the aft (rear). This allows the ballasts to be adjusted to modify the weight distribution of the submersible both up and down, but also forwards and backwards, allowing neutral buoyancy to be achieved. Each ballast will contain an "in" port and an "out" port, usually run through multiple pumps (as shifting ballasts on a single pump can be quite a time consuming task). They can be balanced using [PID controllers](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Logic).

## Airlocks

It can occasionally be necessary to enter or leave a submersible whilst underwater. Using a regular door would cause the submarine to flood and sink. A solution to this problem is the use of an [airlock](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Airlock) to flood only a small section of the vessel then remove the water with a pump.

## See Also

- [Airlocks](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Airlock)
- [Boats](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Boat)
- [Vehicles](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Vehicles)
- [Water Vehicles](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Vehicles/Water)

The world of Stormworks is made up of islands and larger landmasses. The game world of Stormworks is made up of Tiles, which allow for the world to be produced from a seed via procedural generation. The smaller islands often fit into a single tile, while the larger landmasses such as the [Sawyer Islands](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Sawyer_Islands) are made up of multiple tiles. Without modification of the game itself, it is impossible for the tiles making up the larger landmasses to not be generated together. The tiles are generated at the beginning of a save and do not become altered over time.

Some Islands come with [Workbenches](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building#Workbenches), which allow for the construction of vehicles, assuming you have 'purchased' said island. Landmasses come with several sites or locations where workbenches can be utilized.

Other locations are generated around the world such as settlements, wind turbines, oil rigs. Some of these serve a purpose as they support key game mechanics, and others are purely for decoration.

## Landmasses

These landmasses are large islands or groups of islands that always appear in the same place in every game.

- **[Sawyer Islands](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Sawyer_Islands)**: a set of six islands forming a large landmass in the center of the map. It has roads, railways, and airstrips.
- **[Arctic](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Arctic)**: a grouping of small islands to the far north of the map. It is surrounded by icebergs.
- **[Isle of Donkk](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Isle_of_Donkk)**: a chain of islands all connected by railway and road bridges situated to the west of the Sawyer Islands.
- **[Volcanic Chain](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Volcanic_Chain)**: a chain of volcanic islands to the south-west of the Sawyer Islands.
- **[Arid Island](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Arid_Island)**: a large landmass to the south of the map, made up of deserts and mountainous regions. It is the largest landmass in the game, and has many roads and railways. Its presence on the map requires the [Industrial Frontier DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Industrial_Frontier_DLC) to be turned on.

## Outpost and Bases

These areas are places which the player can purchase and then use to create vehicles or structures. The majority of them can also be selected as a spawnpoint for the game.

- **[Coastguard Outpost Beginner](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Coastguard_Outpost_Beginner)** ($10 000): A small island with a small boathouse allowing for the creation of a small boat or submarine. It will always spawn in a pair with the St. Sebastiaz Hospital island. It is the location of the tutorial mission, that is started upon starting a game here.
- **[Coastguard Outpost TT](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Coastguard_Outpost_TT)** ($10 000): A small island with a small hangar and small helipad allowing for the creation of a small VTOL.
- **[Harbour Base](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Harbour_Base)** ($15 000): A small island with a medium-sized dock that allows for the creation of medium-sized boats. It is a natural upgrade to the Coastguard Outpost Beginner.
- **[Airstrip Base](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Airstrip_Base)** ($30 000): A small island with a small hangar and runway allowing for the creation of a small plane.
- **[Terminal Spycakes](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Terminal_Spycakes)** ($40 000): A harbor in the west of the Isle of Donkk allowing for the creation of a large boat, and trains. Named After The youtuber [Spycakes](https://www.youtube.com/spycakes)
- **Fishing Village** ($50 000): A small village in the south-east of the Sawyer Islands. It allows for the construction of a large boat. It also has a gantry that buys diesel.
- **Dreimor Airstrip** ($50 000): An airstrip in the west of the Isle of Donkk allowing for the creation of a large airplane.
- **[North Harbor](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/North_Harbor)** ($60,000): A coastal harbor on the north of the Sawyer Islands, with room for the construction of large boats, and trains.
- **Harrison Airbase** ($80 000): An airstrip with a hangar allowing for the construction of large planes.
- **Terminal Camodo** ($80 000): A harbor in the east of the Isle of Donkk allowing for the construction of a large boat and trains. Named After The Youtuber Named [Camodo Gaming](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCC6ulNJ-KDoIa3VI2gcvQpA)
- **Military Base** ($90 000): A large island with two runways, a large hangar, and a large dock. Large aircraft can be made here, but ships cannot.
- **Custom Base Submarine** ($100 000): A medium-sized island with a hidden cave, allowing for the creation of large submarines. It contains two base construction tables, one in the cave and one on top of the island.
- **Custom Base Heli** ($100 000): A small island with a flat top, allowing for the construction of a base. It does not have any vehicle construction tables.
- **Custom Base Large Boat** ($100 000): A medium-sized island with a base construction table, and space to build a large boat.
- **Custom Base Small Boat** ($100 000): A small island with a base construction table, and space to build a small boat.
- **Custom Base Oil Rig (Large)** ($100 000): A structure allowing for the construction of a custom oil rig. It has an oil deposit underneath the structure.
- **Terminal Endo** ($100 000): A rail yard in the south of the Arctic's main island, allowing for the construction of trains.
- **Terminal Trinite** ($100 000): A rail yard in the north of the Arctic's main island, allowing for the construction of trains.
- **O'Neill Airbase** ($120 000): An airstrip with a hangar allowing for the construction of large planes. It is located near to a train terminal that buys coal.
- **Coastguard Outpost** ($150 000): A large island with a large hangar, runway, and harbor. It's intended for use as a base of operations when playing in custom mode.
- **Tajin Airstrip** ($200 000): A large airstrip in the Arctic, allowing for the construction of airplanes.
- **Multiplayer Base** ($220 000): A large island with a large hangar, two runways, and a dock. The hangar and the dock both allow for the construction of two aircraft and boats at the same time.

The following bases are situated on the Arid Island, and can thus only be used if the [Industrial Frontier DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Industrial_Frontier_DLC) is turned on.

- **North Meier Outpost** ($30 000): A small harbor in the north-west of the Arid Island, with a small dock and garage, allowing the construction of small boats, land vehicles, and VTOLs.
- **Brainz Train Yard** ($45 000): A train yard allowing for the construction of trains.
- **Uran Wind Power Plant** ($230 000): A big harbor in the north of the Arid Island, allowing for the construction of large boats.
- **Serpentine Train Yard** ($60 000): A train yard allowing for the construction of trains.
- **30 Dollar Train Yard** ($60 000): A train yard allowing for the construction of trains.
- **Mauve Train Yard** ($45 000): A train yard allowing for the construction of trains, near to the Lex Truck Stop.
- **JSI Dock** ($80 000): A medium-sized harbor with space to build two large boats.
- **FJ Warner Docks** ($80 000): A large harbor with a train yard and a hangar allowing the construction of large boats, planes, land vehicles, VTOLs and trains.
- **Clarke Airfield + Monkey Brain Launch Site** ($120 000): A large airfield with a large hangar, A large rocket launch site, allowing for the construction of rocket ships and large planes.
- **Endair Airfield** ($140 000): An airfield in the south-west of the Arid Island, with a hangar allowing the construction of airplanes.

### Vehicle Construction Sizes

## Settlements

These are other kinds of settlements, with structures or infrastructure, some with purpose, and some for decoration.

- Sawyer Islands: Fishing Village, Dean Hall Mining Company, Holt Town, Olsen Bay, Wind Farm
- Arctic: ArcTech Survey Base, Arcturus, BVG Freight Terminal, Daylight Oil Refinery, Krail Oilworks, Magnus Shipbreaking Ltd. xFury Drilling Co. and Uranium Processing
- Open Ocean: Brinkfield, Jet Fuel Gantry, Offshore Wind Turbines, Oil Rigs, Sea Fort
- Isle of Donkk: Donkk Coal Mines, Kalopsidiotis Chemical Storage, Lighthouse OB(Named after The Youtube [Beautiful OB](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCgVDjpyBZa8wiSAd9oNi7RQ))
- Arid Islands: Charlizard Train Stop, Chickensaur Gas Station, Chris Ranch, Noah Village, Qwop Town, Raptor Lighthouse, Kenichi Train Stop, Ghost Town, Chaykovsky Town, Gravedigger Truck Stop, Benzin Gas Station, Olli Switch Yard, Keh Storage Facility, Uran Wind Power Plant and Uranium Processing, Expo Village, Lex Truck Stop, Hyanen Garage, Robert Barnsley Observatory, Bubbles Watertower, Karn Industries Factory, Kahrstrom Gas Station, Scxheech Trading Yard, Mallamar Gold Purification Lab, Mass Hole Shaft, Britzilla Uranium Mines, Empire Industries Metal Ore Foundry, Albiebie Train Stop, Lyams Garage, Personnagio Farm, Alijon Farm, Ace Master Gold Dirt Separator, Thomas Train Stop, Kobold Ore Terminal, Hennenberg Old Mine, Kobold Iron Quarry, Keptin Aluminium Terminal, Zizos Gas Station, Enzo Kats Village, Keptin Aluminium Mines, Campbell Lighthouse.

## Underwater features

(This section is very incomplete.)

- Balfour Trench: A pair of outcroppings with a trench between them, the top is only about 40m deep while the bottom is about 80m deep.
- Lothian Basin: A ring of outcroppings. May contain two [loot chests](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Loot_crate) in the center at the bottom. Deepest area is about 90m.
- MRN Jersey: A sunken cargo freighter surrounded by outcroppings. May contain a loot chest. The depth is around 80m.

The world of Stormworks is made up of islands and larger landmasses. The game world of Stormworks is made up of Tiles, which allow for the world to be produced from a seed via procedural generation. The smaller islands often fit into a single tile, while the larger landmasses such as the [[Sawyer Islands]] are made up of multiple tiles. Without modification of the game itself, it is impossible for the tiles making up the larger landmasses to not be generated together. The tiles are generated at the beginning of a save and do not become altered over time.

Some Islands come with [[Wiki/Building#Workbenches|Workbenches]], which allow for the construction of vehicles, assuming you have 'purchased' said island. Landmasses come with several sites or locations where workbenches can be utilized.

Other locations are generated around the world such as settlements, wind turbines, oil rigs. Some of these serve a purpose as they support key game mechanics, and others are purely for decoration.

==Landmasses==
These landmasses are large islands or groups of islands that always appear in the same place in every game.

* '''[[Sawyer Islands]]''': a set of six islands forming a large landmass in the center of the map. It has roads, railways, and airstrips.
* '''[[Arctic]]''': a grouping of small islands to the far north of the map. It is surrounded by icebergs.
* '''[[Isle of Donkk]]''': a chain of islands all connected by railway and road bridges situated to the west of the Sawyer Islands.
* '''[[Volcanic Chain]]''': a chain of volcanic islands to the south-west of the Sawyer Islands.
* '''[[Arid Island]]''': a large landmass to the south of the map, made up of deserts and mountainous regions. It is the largest landmass in the game, and has many roads and railways. Its presence on the map requires the [[Industrial Frontier DLC]] to be turned on.

==Outpost and Bases==
These areas are places which the player can purchase and then use to create vehicles or structures. The majority of them can also be selected as a spawnpoint for the game.

*'''[[Coastguard Outpost Beginner]]''' ($10 000): A small island with a small boathouse allowing for the creation of a small boat or submarine. It will always spawn in a pair with the St. Sebastiaz Hospital island. It is the location of the [[Tutorial Mission|tutorial mission]], that is started upon starting a game here.
*'''[[Coastguard Outpost TT]]''' ($10 000): A small island with a small hangar and small helipad allowing for the creation of a small VTOL.
*'''[[Harbour Base]]''' ($15 000): A small island with a medium-sized dock that allows for the creation of medium-sized boats. It is a natural upgrade to the Coastguard Outpost Beginner.
*'''[[Airstrip Base]]''' ($30 000): A small island with a small hangar and runway allowing for the creation of a small plane.
*'''[[Terminal Spycakes]]''' ($40 000): A harbor in the west of the Isle of Donkk allowing for the creation of a large boat, and trains. Named After The youtuber [https://www.youtube.com/spycakes Spycakes]
*'''Fishing Village''' ($50 000): A small village in the south-east of the Sawyer Islands. It allows for the construction of a large boat. It also has a gantry that buys diesel.
*'''Dreimor Airstrip''' ($50 000): An airstrip in the west of the Isle of Donkk allowing for the creation of a large airplane.
*'''[[North Harbor]]''' ($60,000): A coastal harbor on the north of the Sawyer Islands, with room for the construction of large boats, and trains.
*'''Harrison Airbase''' ($80 000): An airstrip with a hangar allowing for the construction of large planes.
*'''Terminal Camodo''' ($80 000): A harbor in the east of the Isle of Donkk allowing for the construction of a large boat and trains. Named After The Youtuber Named [https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCC6ulNJ-KDoIa3VI2gcvQpA Camodo Gaming]
*'''Military Base''' ($90 000): A large island with two runways, a large hangar, and a large dock. Large aircraft can be made here, but ships cannot.
*'''Custom Base Submarine''' ($100 000): A medium-sized island with a hidden cave, allowing for the creation of large submarines. It contains two base construction tables, one in the cave and one on top of the island.
*'''Custom Base Heli''' ($100 000): A small island with a flat top, allowing for the construction of a base. It does not have any vehicle construction tables.
*'''Custom Base Large Boat''' ($100 000): A medium-sized island with a base construction table, and space to build a large boat.
*'''Custom Base Small Boat''' ($100 000): A small island with a base construction table, and space to build a small boat.
*'''Custom Base Oil Rig (Large)''' ($100 000): A structure allowing for the construction of a custom oil rig. It has an oil deposit underneath the structure.
*'''Terminal Endo''' ($100 000): A rail yard in the south of the Arctic's main island, allowing for the construction of trains.
*'''Terminal Trinite''' ($100 000): A rail yard in the north of the Arctic's main island, allowing for the construction of trains.
*'''O'Neill Airbase''' ($120 000): An airstrip with a hangar allowing for the construction of large planes. It is located near to a train terminal that buys coal.
*'''Coastguard Outpost''' ($150 000): A large island with a large hangar, runway, and harbor. It's intended for use as a base of operations when playing in custom mode.
*'''Tajin Airstrip''' ($200 000): A large airstrip in the Arctic, allowing for the construction of airplanes.
*'''Multiplayer Base''' ($220 000): A large island with a large hangar, two runways, and a dock. The hangar and the dock both allow for the construction of two aircraft and boats at the same time.
